title: mass-type invariants in the presence of a cosmological constant
abstract: in this paper, we introduce a new family of mass-type invariants for time-symmetric initial data in space-times satisfying the dominant energy condition. for positive cosmological constant, these invariants, unlike the total hawking mass, turn out to be genuinely effective in providing new characterizations of the de sitter solution. from a theoretical standpoint, this opens a new perspective on how one might refine the rigidity statement originally proposed by min-oo in his well known conjecture, later refuted by the counterexamples of brendle, marques, and neves. via a formal limiting procedure, we also define another invariant, the 1-harmonic mass, for which we independently prove a positive mass theorem and a penrose-type inequality, thereby extending tools for probing space-time geometries in the presence of a positive cosmological constant.

title: the general-relativistic limit of f(r) gravity
abstract: we establish the general-relativistic limit of f(r) gravity coupled to a massless scalar field for small, asymptotically euclidean, well-prepared cauchy data near minkowski spacetime. we prove global existence and future causal geodesic completeness, with uniform estimates for the metric, matter, and rescaled effective field as an admissible family of modified lagrangians f(r) approaches the einstein-hilbert lagrangian r. the physical and conformal metrics and the matter field converge to the limiting einstein-massless-scalar development, uniformly on the entire future spacetime, together with finitely many space and time derivatives. the effective field, defined by a nonlinear reparametrization of the physical scalar curvature, converges to the scalar curvature of the limiting einstein development. the main analytical difficulty is that the effective-field mass tends to infinity, while its evolution equation becomes an algebraic trace relation. small field amplitudes may coexist with high-frequency oscillations and comparatively large derivatives, whose quadratic contributions must be controlled uniformly. using the euclidean-hyperboloidal foliation method and adapted wave coordinates, we analyze a quasilinear wave-klein-gordon system whose nonlinearities do not satisfy the classical null condition. we combine oscillatory estimates, weighted interior and exterior energies, and propagation estimates for the discrepancy from the einstein trace relation. quantitative convergence on compact regions and uniform spacetime decay yield global convergence.

title: the seeds and silhouettes of optimal gravitational shielding
abstract: we construct complete vacuum initial data sets with prescribed asymptotically flat exterior geometry, including the gluing of two schwarzschild exterior regions with small masses (which need not be positive). the construction allows for arbitrarily slow leading decay and nonzero second fundamental form. for leading terms with a fixed radial power, we first construct localized seed data sets whose constraint errors decay to any prescribed finite order, then apply the projection and stability theorems of our companion papers. the resulting vacuum data sets differ from seeds by harmonic terms controlled by hamiltonian and momentum silhouettes, and by super-harmonic corrections. this difference of harmonic terms is measured by a relative notion of adm energy-momentum, which is defined even for slowly-decaying data sets that do not admit an adm energy-momentum. upon adjusting seed data sets by either harmonic-decaying terms or compact transverse-traceless terms, we freely control this relative adm charge and, when it exists, the total adm charge. in particular, when gluing schwarzschild metrics the total adm mass can be specified independently of the schwarzschild mass parameters. together with our companion papers, these results establish a constructive theory of optimal localization beyond harmonic decay.

title: covariant phase space analysis of static spherical vacua in power-law $f(r)$ gravity
abstract: we formulate the static, spherically symmetric vacuum equations of power-law metric $f(r)$ gravity as a covariant autonomous system using the $(1+1+2)$ formalism. the finite critical sets include the scale-invariant clifton--barrow solution, a minkowski endpoint shared by the schwarzschild family, and degenerate boundaries of the normalized chart. the clifton--barrow equilibrium is an outward-radial attractor over a positive interval of the power-law parameter, whereas the schwarzschild endpoint is a saddle of the polynomially extended system. poincaré compactification, supplemented by secondary and weighted charts, resolves several asymptotic regimes. in particular, normally attracting sheets at large normalized curvature occur in the positive-curvature sector and are separated from the negative-curvature clifton--barrow equilibrium. metric reconstruction also identifies a selected scalar-flat family with a regular throat, one asymptotically flat end, and a curvature-singular end. these results organize the regular reduced chart and the boundary regimes resolved here; they do not constitute a complete classification of static spherical vacua. all stability statements concern the static radial flow.

title: quasinormal-mode encounters: pseudospectra near kerr--newman exceptional points
abstract: exceptional points (eps), at which two quasinormal frequencies and their eigenvectors coalesce, can strongly enhance the spectral instability of black hole quasinormal modes. we investigate this behavior in kerr--newman spacetimes through pseudospectra and condition numbers for neutral massless scalar fields and coupled gravitoelectromagnetic (ge) perturbations. for the scalar field, we follow the $(\ell,m)=(1,1)$ spheroidal branch and derive the energy norm from the stress-energy tensor. for ge perturbations, we use a coupled four-field system equipped with a positive radiative energy. at the selected near-ep backgrounds, the condition numbers of both modes in the close pair exceed those of the two more-damped modes shown for comparison at the same background. along a matched ge parameter path, the frequency splitting follows a square-root law and the condition numbers grow as the inverse square root of the distance to the ep. the pseudospectral contours resolve the transition from individual-mode sensitivity to the collective response of the pair. within the discretized problems and energy norms considered here, these results quantify the amplification of spectral instability near eps and provide a basis for studying their contribution to black-hole ringdown.

title: gravity between two masses beyond newton's law
abstract: newton's law of universal gravitation describes the attraction between two masses through an inverse-distance potential. in einstein's theory gravity gravitates: each mass reshapes the spacetime geometry through which the other acts. more than a century later, extracting the two-body interaction from this coupled geometry remains a fundamental analytical challenge. even without motion or radiation, the static sector of the interaction harbours an infinite hierarchy of field couplings: the purest laboratory for gravitational non-linearity. here we determine the static interaction from ninth to twelfth order in newton's constant for arbitrary mass ratios, and derive a closed expression for the first backreaction beyond the schwarzschild test-body limit to all orders in the gravitational coupling. we achieve both advances by formulating the problem around the stationary interaction energy. an exact one-body background resums one source's self-interaction, stationarity reduces the fields required from the other, and integrated response identities reveal cancellations across the coupled modes. complementary expansions then resolve the complete mass dependence at finite order. together, these results bridge the gap between an infinitesimal probe and comparable masses, exposing hidden analytical simplicity within einstein's theory and providing essential building blocks for modelling orbital dynamics and gravitational-wave generation.

title: centro-affine differential geometry and the log-minkowski problem
abstract: we interpret the log-brunn-minkowski conjecture of böröczky-lutwak-yang-zhang as a spectral problem in centro-affine differential geometry. in particular, we show that the hilbert-brunn-minkowski operator coincides with the centro-affine laplacian, thus obtaining a new avenue for tackling the conjecture using insights from affine differential geometry. as every strongly convex hypersurface in $\mathbb{r}^n$ is a centro-affine unit-sphere, it has constant centro-affine ricci curvature equal to $n-2$, in stark contrast to the standard weighted ricci curvature of the associated metric-measure space, which will in general be negative. in particular, we may use the classical argument of lichnerowicz and a centro-affine bochner formula to give a new proof of the brunn-minkowski inequality. for origin-symmetric convex bodies enjoying fairly generous curvature pinching bounds (improving with dimension), we are able to show global uniqueness in the $l^p$- and log-minkowski problems, as well as the corresponding global $l^p$- and log-minkowski conjectured inequalities. as a consequence, we resolve the isomorphic version of the log-minkowski problem: for any origin-symmetric convex body $\bar k$ in $\mathbb{r}^n$, there exists an origin-symmetric convex body $k$ with $\bar k \subset k \subset 8 \bar k$, so that $k$ satisfies the log-minkowski conjectured inequality, and so that $k$ is uniquely determined by its cone-volume measure $v_k$. if $\bar k$ is not extremely far from a euclidean ball to begin with, an analogous isometric result, where $8$ is replaced by $1+ε$, is obtained as well.

title: fractal dimension of singular times for spdes: energy bounds, criticality, and weak-strong uniqueness
abstract: for several physically relevant spdes, it is known that global weak solutions coexist with local strong ones. typically, weak-strong uniqueness results are known, and ensure that the global and strong solutions coincide as long as the latter exist. times at which a weak solution does not coincide with a strong one are called singular times. determining their fractal dimension is fundamental to capturing the regularity of weak solutions.   we introduce a probabilistic notion of singular times for a wide class of semilinear spdes. we show that sets of singular times have fractal dimension (i.e., hausdorff and/or minkowski) at most $ 1-\ell\, \mathsf{exc}$, where $\ell$ and $\mathsf{exc}$ are the time integrability and the excess of spatial regularity compared to the critical regularity of the energy bound associated with weak solutions, respectively. moreover, their corresponding $(1-\ell\,\mathsf{exc} )$-dimensional measure is zero. we formulate and apply our theory to annealed strong leray-hopf solutions of 3d navier-stokes equations (nses) with physically relevant noises, including rough kraichnan and lie transport. in particular, we extend the fundamental $1/2$-dimensional bound of leray and scheffer on singular times for 3d nses to the stochastic setting, and we prove new conditional results under supercritical serrin's conditions, irrespective of the roughness of the noise. our framework is new even in the deterministic case, and provides the first partial regularity results for weak solutions to spdes with multiplicative noise.

title: noether symmetries and conservation laws of a class of time-dependent multidimensional nonlinear wave equations
abstract: conservation laws of a class of time-dependent damped nonlinear multidimensional wave equations are derived by noether's theorem. for arbitrary nonzero damping coefficient and nonlinear interaction term, its infinitesimal variational symmetries span a euclidean algebra $\euclid(n)$ of space translations and rotations. they produce conservation of linear and angular momentums. for some specific forms of these two terms symmetry algebra is enlarged to a subalgebra of the conformal algebra $\conf(1,n)$ and in this case more interesting conservation laws are found.

title: brownian motion in minkowski normed spaces
abstract: a minkowski normed space is the euclidean space equipped with a (possibly asymmetric) uniformly convex and smooth norm, forming a particular class of finsler manifolds.   we construct a stochastic process with one-dimensional time marginal densities given by the fundamental solution to the nonlinear finsler heat equation in minkowski normed spaces.   this process is constructed as a solution to a singular mckean--vlasov stochastic differential equation and constitutes a nonlinear markov process in the sense of mckean.   we show that solutions to this stochastic differential equation are pathwise unique, and, thus, probabilistically strong solutions, though the equation has singular coefficients beyond the subcritical regime.   since our construction is a natural extension of the construction of standard brownian motion from the standard heat kernel, we call this process \emph{brownian motion in minkowski normed spaces.}   furthermore, we obtain a universality property, namely that whichever minkowski norm is chosen, the radial part of this process is the standard bessel process.   to the best of our knowledge, this is the first construction of stochastic processes associated with nonlinear heat equation in finslerian spaces.

title: blow up and concentration without quantization: sharp harnack type inequalities
abstract: motivated by the onsager statistical mechanics description of turbulent euler flows with point singularities, we refine the blow up analysis for sequences of solutions of a class of perturbed singular liouville equations which share the phenomenon of ``blow up and concentration without quantization". the problem is delicate because we are dealing with the exact threshold value above which one meets the well known ``concentration without quantization" phenomenon, as recently pushed forward in [c.s. lin, g. tarantello, {\em c. r. math. acad. sci. paris} (2016)] and in [y. lee, c.s. lin, g. tarantello, w. yang, {\em comm. pde.} (2017)]. we overcome these difficulties by developing different strategies for ``fast" and ``slow" blow up, combining refined pohozaev identities, elliptic estimates and ``sup+cinf" inequalities in the same spirit of [c.c. chen, c.s. lin, {\em comm. an. geom.} (1998)]. in the process, we also derive a new sharp harnack type inequality by using a moving-plane method, following the ideas in [d. bartolucci, c.c. chen, c.s. lin, g. tarantello, {\em comm. p.d.e.} (2002)].

title: an alternative variational approach to constrained critical points for nonlinear schrödinger equations with combined nonlinearities
abstract: we introduce a new variational framework for the study of standing waves for nonlinear schrödinger equations with combined power nonlinearities. the approach is based on minimizing the mass functional over a set defined by an upper bound on the energy and a lower bound on a nonlinear potential term, rather than minimizing the energy at prescribed mass. this yields a new characterization of the sharp gagliardo--nirenberg optimizer through purely variational constraints. as a consequence, we establish the existence of minimizers for all energy levels below a critical threshold and derive the corresponding euler--lagrange equations. these minimizers give rise to standing-wave solutions of the nonlinear schröedinger equation

title: an introduction to the obstacle problem
abstract: we give a self-contained account of the classical obstacle problem, written for graduate students who wish to enter the field of free boundary problems. starting from a one-dimensional model and an explicit radially symmetric example, we set up the variational problem, show that minimizers exist and are unique, and prove interior $w^{2,p}$-regularity as well as the optimal $c^{1,1}$-regularity. the second half of the notes is devoted to the free boundary: we prove that it is porous, introduce blow-up limits, and use the alt-caffarelli-friedman monotonicity formula to show that every free boundary point is either regular or singular. these notes grew out of a mini-course at the rio summer school on pdes in 2020, and they are meant to be read alongside, not instead of, the monograph by petrosyan, shahgholian, and uraltseva.

title: classification of threshold dynamics for the focusing mass-critical inhomogeneous nls
abstract: we study the focusing mass-critical inhomogeneous nonlinear schrödinger equation $i\partial_{t}u+δu+|x|^{-b}|u|^{\frac{4-2b}{d}}u=0$ in dimensions $d\ge3$. for $\frac12<b<\min\{2,d/2\}$, we prove that every forward-global $h^1$ solution with mass equal to that of the ground state $q$ either scatters forward or coincides with $e^{it}q$, up to phase rotation and scaling. as a consequence, every solution with nonradial $h^1$ initial data at the ground-state mass must be global and scatter in both time directions. for $0<b\le\frac12$, analogous rigidity and scattering results hold under an additional finite-variance assumption. the key new ingredients in our proof are a nonradial incoming/outgoing decomposition and exterior frequency-decay estimates, which yield the kinetic-energy localization needed for a localized virial argument.

title: asymptotic formula of the lifespan of classical solutions to 1d quasilinear wave equations
abstract: we study the lifespan \(t^*(\varepsilon)\) of classical solutions to the cauchy problem   for the one-dimensional quasilinear wave equation   $u_{tt}-(c(u)^2u_x)_x=0$,   with initial data of size $\varepsilon>0$.   we assume that $c'(θ)\sim a|θ|^{p-2}$ as $θ\to 0$,   where \(a>0\) and \(p>3\) or $p=2$.   we obtain explicit asymptotic formulas for   $t^*(\varepsilon)$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$.   we treat both the case $ψ\in l^1(\mathbb r)$   and the case   $ψ=ψ_1+\braket{x}^{-α}$,   where \(ψ_1\in l^1(\mathbb r)\) and \(0<α\le1\).   our results identify the dependence of the lifespan scale on the decay exponent,   including the borderline case $α=1$.   the proof combines riccati equations along characteristics   with a scaling argument inspired by lindblad.

title: a fully nonlinear parabolic segregation problem
abstract: we study a two-phase parabolic free boundary problem arising as the segregation limit of a competition-diffusion system with strong interactions and fully nonlinear diffusion. the positive and negative phases are governed by different equations and are coupled through global viscosity inequalities. we construct viscosity solutions that are lipschitz in space and $1/2$-hölder in time, and establish differentiability in space across the free boundary, including at singular points. at regular points, we prove that the solution has a parabolic $c^{1,α}$ asymptotic expansion, and deduce that the free boundary is locally a $c^{1,α}$ hypersurface. the proof relies on a parabolic alt-caffarelli-friedman monotonicity formula to classify blow-up limits, followed by an improvement of flatness argument.

title: low-regularity global well-posedness for the defocusing cubic wave equation outside a ball with radial initial data
abstract: we study the three-dimensional defocusing cubic nonlinear wave equation with homogeneous dirichlet boundary condition in the exterior of the unit ball, $ω=\r^3\backslash\overline{b(0,1)}$, for radial initial data. for every $\frac12\leq s\leq\frac34$, we establish global well-posedness in $\dot h^s_{d,rad}(ω)\times\dot h^{s-1}_{d,rad}(ω)$, including the critical endpoint $s=\frac12$, without an additional $l^4$ assumption on the initial displacement. the proof uses the distorted fourier transform associated with the dirichlet laplacian to establish radial sobolev embeddings, including the quantitative estimate $\|f\|_{l^p(ω)}\leq c\sqrt p\,\|f\|_{\dot h_d^{1/2}(ω)}$ for $4\leq p<\infty$, with $c$ independent of $p$. we combine a nonlinear fourier truncation argument with the critical strichartz estimate to construct a global nonlinear component with high-frequency-truncated initial data. for the remainder, we construct a local energy solution in an affine energy space and derive a logarithmic energy inequality that prevents finite-time energy blow-up. persistence of the original sobolev regularity, uniqueness, and local lipschitz dependence on each finite time interval complete the proof.

title: electromagnetic potentials via the extended maxwell system
abstract: we construct electromagnetic potentials on arbitrary open 3-dimensional sets for anisotropic, non-homogeneous materials, thus rendering any topological assumption like simple connectedness or the absence of holes superfluous in this context. the main idea is to invoke the extended maxwell system the easy solution theory of which then yields existence of both scalar- and vector potentials.

title: equal diffusions and zero dirichlet boundary conditions can induce blow-up
abstract: for a class of systems of two parabolic equations with equal diffusion and homogeneous dirichlet boundary conditions, we show the existence of finite time blow-up solutions, although the corresponding system of ode's has only global, exponentially decaying solutions. such a phenomenon of blow-up induced by equal diffusions, which originates in the works of bebernes-lacey [siam j. math. anal. 21 (1990), 1415--1425, and j. differential equations 95 (1992), 105--129] and weinberger [j. differ. equations 154 (1999), 225--237], was previously known, for instance, in the case of homogeneous neumann boundary conditions, but it had remained an open question whether it can happen in the homogeneous dirichlet case. the latter, which corresponds to an absorption or cooling of the system at the boundary, that is a priori more stabilizing, requires nontrivial new ideas. as another new feature, we show that this can happen even if the nonlinearity acts only on a compact sub-region, and our proof actually covers the neumann and cauchy, as well as dirichlet problems in a unified way.

title: analysis of blowup masses in constant-coefficient toda systems: w-invariants and weyl orbits
abstract: we classify the local blowup masses of constant-coefficient toda systems for all simple lie algebras with one prescribed singular source, bounded component masses, and bounded boundary oscillations. we encode the source strengths and the blowup masses by two elements of the cartan subalgebra: the grading element $p_μ$ and the mass element $q_σ$. we show that $p_μ-q_σ=wp_μ$ for some weyl group element $w\in w$. the proof uses the drinfeld-sokolov gauge and the resulting holomorphic $w$-invariants for toda systems. asymptotic analysis near the source and on a shrinking circle enclosing the total local mass gives two evaluations of the leading laurent coefficients of the $w$-invariants, which agree by holomorphicity. this agreement enables us to conclude the above weyl-orbit result. in particular, the quadratic constraint is the local pohozaev identity. only with the full set of $w$-invariants can we strengthen earlier orbit-plus-integer restrictions to an exact weyl-orbit characterization in the constant-coefficient setting. together with the author's explicit families in [nie], this determines all attainable local mass vectors.

title: suppression of the benjamin-feir instability by constant vorticity
abstract: we study the effect of constant vorticity on the benjamin-feir instability of small-amplitude stokes waves in infinite depth. working with the full water-wave equations, we rigorously establish a transition between modulational instability and stability as the vorticity crosses a critical value. we consider right-propagating waves with constant vorticity $γ$, associated with the background shear current $-γy\mathbf e_x$, and normalize the gravitational acceleration and carrier wavenumber to one. for each fixed $γ<2/\sqrt{3}$, we prove that sufficiently small-amplitude stokes waves are benjamin-feir unstable. for each fixed $γ>2/\sqrt{3}$, these waves are spectrally stable with respect to longitudinal, long-wavelength perturbations. these results rigorously confirm, away from the critical value, the stability transition predicted by the formal nonlinear schrödinger approximation of thomas, kharif, and manna.

title: a paley-wiener-type theorem with applications to inverse medium scattering for the schrödinger equation
abstract: this paper develops a new uniqueness framework for inverse scattering problems for the time-harmonic schrödinger equation using multi-frequency data. our approach is based on a paley-wiener-type theorem that characterizes the support of the potential through the asymptotic growth of a generalized fourier integral along imaginary frequencies, allowing for nontrivial amplitude functions.   within this framework, we obtain two major results on identifying the shape of the support of the potential in three dimensions, for both the plane-wave incidence and point source incidence, respectively. for plane-wave incidence, we prove that the location and shape of the convex compact support of an essentially bounded potential are uniquely determined by fixed-angle far-field data from two opposite incident directions or by backscattering far field data, provided that the potential is real-valued and sign-definite near the boundary of its support. for point-source incidence, we show that near-field backscattering data, namely the scattered field evaluated at the source point as the source ranges over a sufficiently large sphere, uniquely determine the location and shape of the convex support under the same assumptions on the potential. the proofs rely on meromorphic extension and the paley-wiener-type theorem.

title: power-type nonlinear schrödinger equations with the logarithmic laplacian
abstract: we prove global existence of the cauchy problem of a schrodinger equation with the logarithmic laplacian and a pure power linearity. we address the focusing and the defocusing cases, and we obtained a sharp blow-up in time result.

title: classification of anti-symmetric solutions to fractional lane-emden system in borderline case
abstract: we investigate the existence and non-existence of anti-symmetric solutions to the fractional lane--emden system in the half-space $\mathbb{r}^n_+$:   \begin{equation*}\begin{cases}   (-δ)^s u = v^p & \text{in } \mathbb{r}^n_+,   (-δ)^s v = u^q & \text{in } \mathbb{r}^n_+,   \end{cases}\end{equation*}   where $0<s<\frac{1}{2},p,q>0,2s+p=1$, with $u,v$ nonnegative in $\mathbb{r}^n_+$ and anti-symmetric with respect to $\partial\mathbb{r}^n_+$. li and zhuo [2023, sci. china math.] previously proved non-existence in $l_{2s}$, as well as non-existence in the extended space $l_{2s+1}$ when $1-2s<p,q<\frac{n+2s}{n-2s}$ and existence in $l_{2s+1}$ when $p+2s<1,q+2s<1$. in this paper, we fill the remaining borderline case $p=1-2s$ in $l_{2s+1}$ space. we establish a non-existence result for $1-2s=p\leq q\leq\frac{n+2s}{n-2s}$ and an existence result for $0<q<p=1-2s$. for the non-existence result, we combine a maximum principle for anti-symmetric functions with the method of moving planes to derive a liouville--type theorem when $1-2s<q\leq\frac{n+2s}{n-2s}$. we then iterate the lower-bound estimates to obtain a contradiction through blow-up. to prove the existence of nontrivial solutions when $0<q<1-2s$, we construct a nonhomogeneous solution by a monotone iteration scheme in $l_{2s+1}$ as well as analyze a homogeneous profile. surprisingly, the homogeneous profile serves as a universal lower bound for all solutions.

title: unstable radial equilibria as sharp concentration thresholds for the jäger--luckhaus model on the unit disk
abstract: we identify unstable radial equilibria as sharp concentration thresholds for the jäger--luckhaus chemotaxis system on the unit disk with no-flux boundary conditions. concentration is compared through cumulative mass. at fixed total mass, every radial initial profile more concentrated than an unstable equilibrium produces finite-time blow-up, whereas every nonstationary profile less concentrated than that equilibrium generates a global, uniformly bounded solution converging to the least concentrated radial equilibrium. we also classify the radial equilibria and determine their nonlinear stability. let $λ= j_{1,1}^{2}$, where $j_{1,1}$ is the first positive zero of the bessel function $j_1$. for $m\ne λπ$, the least concentrated equilibrium is the unique locally asymptotically stable equilibrium under mass-preserving radial perturbations. it is spatially homogeneous for $m<λπ$ and strictly increasing for $m>λπ$. every other radial equilibrium, including the homogeneous state at $m=λπ$, is nonlinearly unstable. these results clarify how total population and initial spatial aggregation jointly determine collapse or bounded redistribution, and how stable peripheral enrichment can occur within the radial model.

title: linearize or discretize first? error estimates under mesh-uniform regularity and exponential stability for the kdv equation with boundary dissipation
abstract: we study the korteweg-de vries equation on a bounded interval with boundary dissipation, and its spatial semidiscretization by a weighted cubic hermite galerkin method. a small nonlinear wave can be approximated by a linear discrete simulation in two orders: linearize first and then discretize, or discretize first and then linearize. both orders give the same total error, but they divide it differently between linearization and discretization. the difference of the two divisions is the ordering error. we show that it is quadratic in the size of the initial datum and carries a positive power of the mesh size, for all time.   for the continuous problem, the solution map is analytic, with a power series that converges for all time in exponentially weighted trajectory norms. the linearized semigroup has crandall-pazy regularity with the exact index 3/2. for the weighted scheme, exponential stability, kato smoothing, crandall-pazy regularity and analyticity of the solution maps hold uniformly in the mesh size.   these properties give error estimates in which the error and the datum are measured in the same norm: in the energy norm, in $h_0^1$ and in $h^2$. in exponentially weighted time-integrated norms the semidiscrete solutions converge uniformly on balls, at the rate $h^{1/6}$ in $l^4(0,\infty;l^2)$ for data in $l^2$ and at the rate $h^{2/3}$ in $l^2(0,\infty;h^1)$ for data in $h_0^1$. on every interval $[t_0,\infty)$, $t_0>0$, same-norm convergence holds uniformly on balls at algebraic rates. the ordering error is of order $h^{1/6}$ times the square of the energy norm of the datum, uniformly for all $t\ge0$. for the unweighted scheme, a grid wave packet of zero group velocity destroys mesh-uniform kato smoothing and crandall-pazy regularity.

title: normalized solutions and small mass asymptotics for a nonlinear dirac equation with a singular weight and competing powers
abstract: we study normalized solutions of the nonlinear dirac equation \[ \begin{cases} -iα\cdot\nabla u+mβu=μu+|x|^{-b}\bigl(|u|^{q-2}-|u|^{p-2}\bigr)u&\text{in }\mathbb{r}^3,\\ \displaystyle\int_{\mathbb{r}^3}|u|^2\,dx=a, \end{cases} \] where $m>0$, $0<b<1$, $2<q<3-b$, and $q<p<\infty$. for each fixed $p>q$ and all sufficiently small $a>0$, we prove the existence of a normalized solution $(u_a,μ_a)$ with $u_a\in h^1(\mathbb{r}^3;\mathbb c^4)\cap l^\infty(\mathbb{r}^3;\mathbb c^4)$ and $μ_a\in(0,m)$. this covers the weighted sobolev critical and supercritical ranges $p\ge3-b$. our method combines a mass-preserving spectral reduction with a convex truncation and uniform $l^\infty$ estimates. for solutions arising from reduced minimization, we determine the energy asymptotics and the rate at which $μ_a$ approaches $m$ as $a\to0^+$. after rescaling, the upper two-component spinors converge in $h^{\frac12}(\mathbb{r}^3;\mathbb c^2)$ to the set of normalized ground states of a weighted nonlinear schrödinger equation with exponent $q$, while the lower two-component spinors converge to zero in the same space. we also derive an asymptotic formula in $l^2(\mathbb{r}^3;\mathbb c^2)$ for the rescaled lower two-component spinor in terms of the gradient of the limiting schrödinger ground state.

title: sharp observation time for wave equations with an inverse-square boundary potential
abstract: we determine the sharp observation-time threshold for the autonomous, pure-potential wave equation with an inverse-square boundary singularity on the unit ball. for every fixed $κ<0$, full-boundary observability holds on $(-t,t)$ whenever $t>1$ and fails when $t<1$. this resolves, for this model, the optimal-time question raised by enciso, shao, and vergara [j. eur. math. soc. 23 (2021), 3459--3495] and extends their parameter range $-\frac12<κ<0$ to all $κ<0$, including the limit-point regime $κ\leq-\frac12$.   our approach is based on the ingham--beurling theory of nonharmonic fourier series. spherical harmonic decomposition reduces the problem to one-dimensional singular operators, for which we establish frequency separation, local counting estimates, and lower bounds for the boundary norming constants, uniformly in the angular parameter. a quantitative ingham--beurling inequality then yields the sharp-time observability estimate.   as a by-product, this spectral approach provides an independent proof of boundary observability and an explicit functional characterization of its maximal $l^2$ observation domain. the latter is described by a weighted $\ell^2$ condition on the spectral coefficients and consists precisely of energy solutions whose distributional neumann trace belongs to $l^2$. it contains the boundary-admissible energy solutions considered in enciso--shao--vergara's original work.

title: approximation of the relaxed euler system at the level of the compressible navier-stokes equations
abstract: we study the global well-posedness of the cauchy problem in $\mathbb r^d$, $d\geq2$, for the relaxed compressible euler system with a maxwell-type constitutive law for the stress tensor. we show that the corresponding compressible navier-stokes solutions serve as both relaxation limits and large-time asymptotic profiles of the global relaxed euler solutions constructed here. given a navier-stokes background satisfying suitable boundedness and decay assumptions, we construct global smooth relaxed euler solutions for each fixed $α\in(0,1]$ and sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$. here, the background need not be small. after subtracting the stress initial layer, the approximation error is $o(\varepsilon^α)$ uniformly in time. under suitable additional conditions on the initial perturbations, this error decays in $l^2$ faster than the decay of standard navier-stokes background, uniformly in $\varepsilon$, identifying the background solution as a large-time asymptotic profile. as an application, we obtain the corresponding small-data results using classical navier-stokes theory to verify the background assumptions.

title: a transfer principle for elliptic carleman estimates: application to discrete calderón stability
abstract: we develop a transfer principle that lifts continuous elliptic carleman estimates to mesh-uniform estimates for conforming galerkin discretizations. the main difficulties are twofold: discrete states generally lack the \(h^2\)-regularity required by the continuous estimate, and the carleman parameter \(s\) must be controlled relative to the mesh size \(h\). we overcome both by introducing a shifted continuous problem whose galerkin solution is exactly the conforming reconstruction of a prescribed discrete state. weighted approximation then transfers the inequality back to the original discrete operator without adding stabilization, and yields the range \(s\le ch^{-4/5}\) for radial weights. we verify the framework for piecewise affine finite elements with consistent or lumped mass on fitted, uniformly shape-regular meshes, and for standard cartesian finite differences through their finite-element realization. as an application, we study the discrete calderón problem for bounded complex schrödinger potentials in dimension \(d\ge3\). assuming agreement in a fixed connected boundary neighborhood and uniform stability of the discrete dirichlet problems, we obtain stability from dirichlet inputs and variational flux observations on independently prescribed, possibly disjoint boundary patches. the resulting estimate in \(h^{-r}\), \(r>d/2\), retains the single logarithmic data term and the \(o(h^{1/2})\) mesh remainder of the full-data estimate.

title: klein-gordon-born-infeld equations driven by mixed local-nonlocal operators
abstract: in this paper we study a class of klein-gordon-born-infeld systems in which the classical laplacian appearing in the matter equation is replaced by a mixed local-nonlocal operator, whose nonlocal part is allowed to be nonpositive definite according to a real parameter. both the approximate and the exact born-infeld field equations are considered in parallel. after making the functional framework explicit, we identify a range of real parameters for which infinitely many radially symmetric standing waves exist, obtained as mountain pass critical points of the associated reduced energy functionals. the mixed local-nonlocal operator reduces to the classical laplacian as the nonlocal weight vanishes, and is motivated, in the spirit of effective field theories, by nonlocal corrections to the matter dispersion relation.

title: instability theory of stationary solutions for nonlinear schrödinger equations
abstract: we study the orbital instability of algebraically decaying stationary solutions of nonlinear schrödinger equations in dimensions $d\ge2$, taking competing double-power nonlinearities as a canonical model. at zero frequency, the essential spectrum of the linearized operator touches zero, and the usual $h^1$ coercivity is lost. we construct the zero-frequency limit $η_0$ of the frequency derivatives $\partial_ωϕ_ω$ of standing-wave profiles and determine its sharp asymptotic behavior. for a stationary ground state $ϕ_0\in h^1(\mathbb{r}^d)$, we prove instability if $\langle x\rangle\,ϕ_0\notin l^2(\mathbb{r}^d)$ or, when $\langle x\rangle\,ϕ_0\in l^2(\mathbb{r}^d)$, if the duality pairing $\langleη_0,ϕ_0\rangle$ is negative. this criterion is a zero-frequency counterpart of the negative slope condition in the grillakis--shatah--strauss theory. the proof combines variation of parameters for the linearized ode with a shooting analysis that determines the global behavior of the homogeneous solution regular at the origin. we then localize $η_0$ to construct an unstable direction and establish instability through a lyapunov functional argument based on the variational characterization of ground states. the results extend with essentially the same proofs to a class of multiple-power nonlinearities.

title: $γ$-valued stein--tomas restriction for schatten classes
abstract: let $σ\subset\mathbb r^3$ be a compact $c^2$ hypersurface with nonvanishing gaussian curvature. we prove the sharp matrix-dimension-independent schatten-valued stein--tomas range \[ r_σ:l^p(\mathbb r^3;s^a)\longrightarrowγ(l^2(σ),s^a), \qquad 1<a<\infty,\quad 1\le p\le\min\{a,4/3\}. \] the core endpoint is $e_σ:γ(l^2(σ),s^4)\to l^4(\mathbb r^3;s^4)$. after squaring the quartic norm, multiplication lands in the hilbert--schmidt class. a local coarea argument splits resonant quartets according to the shorter adjacent frequency chord, producing a dimension-free row/column estimate for elliptic and hyperbolic curvature. we also show that gaussian type $4/3$ alone does not characterize the corresponding endpoint for arbitrary banach spaces. applications include matrix herglotz waves, a two-dimensional schrödinger $l^4$ estimate, and free spectral-measure bounds.

title: sharp $l^2$ stability for anisotropic radial caffarelli-kohn-nirenberg inequalities
abstract: we establish quantitative stability for radial caffarelli-kohn-nirenberg inequalities involving the anisotropic radial derivative and the minkowski functional of a smooth, strictly convex body in $\mathbb r^n$, $n\ge2$. here, the convex body need not be origin-symmetric. for the $l^2$-caffarelli-kohn-nirenberg inequality, we establish the sharp stability constant $|b+1-a|$ for $a\ne b+1$, and classify all equality cases in the natural weighted completion spaces, by optimizing over the angular coefficients and a common dilation parameter. we also obtain the sharp stability constants $2$ and $4$ for the scale-invariant and scale-noninvariant $l^2$-heisenberg inequality, respectively. for $2\le p<\infty$, we also establish weighted stability of the anisotropic radial $l^p$-caffarelli-kohn-nirenberg inequalities when $a\neq b+1$ and $(b+1-a)(n-p(b+1))\geq0$, and the anisotropic radial $l^p$-heisenberg inequalities. as a byproduct, we establish weighted $l^p$-poincaré inequalities for gamma measures, which serve as the main tool for our stability estimates.

title: sharp lifespan estimates for heat equations with hörmander operators
abstract: in this paper, we study the cauchy problem $u_t-\mathcal l u=h(t)u^p$, $u(0)=\varepsilon u_0\ge0$, where $p>1$, $h\ge0$ is only locally integrable, and $\mathcal l=\sum_{j=1}^mx_j^2$ is a homogeneous hörmander sum of squares on $\mathbb r^n$ of homogeneous dimension $q$. diffusion spreads the solution out and weakens the nonlinearity, while the reaction $h(t)u^p$ may force blow-up. we prove that the outcome is decided by the single quantity $\mathcal{h}_{p,h}(t)=\int_0^th(t)(1+t)^{-\frac q2(p-1)}\,d t$, in which the reaction at time $t$ is weighted by the factor by which diffusion has weakened the solution: small data are global if $\mathcal{h}_{p,h}(\infty)<\infty$, while otherwise the lifespan $t_\varepsilon$ satisfies $c\,\varepsilon^{-(p-1)}\le\mathcal{h}_{p,h}(t_\varepsilon)\le c\,\varepsilon^{-(p-1)}$ for small $\varepsilon$. our technique of proof is based on a backward-semigroup functional combined with a gaussian-envelope energy and an ode cap telescoped along interlaced geometric grids. the result contains the euclidean, heisenberg, carnot and grushin cases, yields explicit lifespan laws for power, logarithmic, exponential, periodic and intermittent coefficients, and exhibits effects with no autonomous counterpart, such as a lifespan with no power law in $\varepsilon$. we also prove regularity and a priori estimates for classical solutions and discuss what remains true for a general nonlinearity $f(u)$.

title: time-domain metric reconstruction for hyperbolic scattering
abstract: self-force methods can be applied in calculations of the scatter angle in two-body hyperbolic encounters, working order by order in the mass ratio (assumed small) but with no recourse to a weak-field approximation. this, in turn, can inform ongoing efforts to construct an accurate model of the general-relativistic binary dynamics via an effective-one-body description and other semi-analytical approaches. existing self-force methods are to a large extent specialised to bound, inspiral orbits. here we develop a technique for (numerical) self-force calculations that can efficiently tackle scatter orbits. the method is based on a time-domain reconstruction of the metric perturbation from a scalar-like hertz potential that satisfies the teukolsky equation, an idea pursued so far only for bound orbits. the crucial ingredient in this formulation are certain jump conditions that (each multipole mode of) the hertz potential must satisfy along the orbit, in a 1+1-dimensional multipole reduction of the problem. we obtain a closed-form expression for these jumps, for an arbitrary geodesic orbit in schwarzschild spacetime, and present a full numerical implementation for a scatter orbit. in this paper we focus on method development, and go only as far as calculating the hertz potential; a calculation of the self-force and its physical effects on the scatter orbit will be the subject of forthcoming work.

title: self-force in hyperbolic black hole encounters
abstract: self-force methods can be applied in calculations of the scatter angle in two-body hyperbolic encounters, working order by order in the mass ratio (assumed small) but with no recourse to a weak-field approximation. this, in turn, can inform ongoing efforts to construct an accurate description of the general-relativistic binary dynamics via an effective-one-body description or other approaches. existing self-force methods are to a large extent specialised to bound, inspiral orbits. here we derive the first-order conservative self-force correction to the scattering angle, show its agreement with recent post-minkowsian results, and develop a technique for (numerical) self-force calculations that can efficiently tackle scatter orbits. in the method, the metric perturbation is reconstructed from a hertz potential that satisfies (mode-by-mode) a certain inhomogeneous version of the teukolsky equation. the crucial ingredient in this formulation are certain jump conditions that the (multipole modes of the) hertz potential must satisfy along the worldline of the small body's orbit. we present a closed-form expression for these jumps, for an arbitrary geodesic orbit in schwarzschild spacetime. to begin developing the numerical infrastructure, a scalar-field evolution code on a schwarzschild background (in 1+1d) is developed. following this, results for the conservative scalar self-force corrections to the scatter angle are calculated. we continue by constructing a teukolsky evolution code on a schwarzschild background. this produces numerically unstable solutions due to unphysical homogeneous solutions of the teukolsky equation at the horizon and null infinity being seeded by numerical error. this can be resolved by a change of variables to a regge-wheeler-like field. we then present a full numerical implementation of this method for circular and scatter orbits in schwarzschild.

title: introduction to the adm formalism
abstract: the authors present concepts and mathematical developments which give rise to the hamiltonian formulation of einstein's general relativity, first introduced by arnowitt, deser, and misner. all the geometrical quantities needed for the construction are explicitly obtained, and examples of some of the application of the formalism are given.

title: multi-generational black hole population analysis with an astrophysically informed mass function
abstract: we analyze the population statistics of black holes in the ligo/virgo/kagra gwtc-3 catalog using a parametric mass function derived from simulations of massive stars experiencing pulsational pair-instability supernovae (ppisn). our formalism enables us to separate the black hole mass function into sub-populations corresponding to mergers between objects formed via different astrophysical pathways, allowing us to infer the properties of black holes formed from stellar collapse and black holes formed via prior mergers separately. applying this formalism, we find that this model fits the data better than the powerlaw+peak model with bayes factor $ 9.7\pm0.1$. we measure the location of the lower edge of the upper black hole mass gap to be $m_{\rm bhmg}=84.05_{-12.88}^{+17.19}{\rm m}_{\odot}$, providing evidence that the $35{\rm m}_{\odot}$ gaussian peak detected in the data using other models is not associated with the ppisn pile-up predicted to precede this gap. incorporating spin, we find that the normalized spins of stellar remnant black holes are close to zero while those of higher generation black holes tend to larger values. all of these results are in accordance with the predictions of stellar structure theory and black hole merger scenarios. finally, we combine our mass function with the spectral siren method for measuring the hubble constant to find $h_0=36.19_{-10.91}^{17.50}$ km/s/mpc and discuss potential explanations of this low value. our results demonstrate how astrophysically-informed mass functions can facilitate the interpretation of gravitational wave catalog data to provide information about black hole formation and cosmology. future data releases will improve the precision of our measurements.

title: quasinormal ringing of de sitter braneworlds
abstract: compared with the poincaré braneworld, the de sitter (ds) braneworld aligns more closely with the present universe characterized by a small but finite cosmological constant; to explore the quasinormal ringing properties within the ds brane scenario, we investigate gravitational perturbations in both thin and thick ds brane configurations. analysis of the perturbation equations reveals that the effective potential along the extra dimension exhibits the shape of a pöschl-teller potential, asymptotically approaching a constant value (mass gap) at infinity, and in particular this mass gap can be reduced. analytical calculations further indicate that the gravitational perturbations, apart from the zero mode, possess a series of discrete, purely imaginary quasinormal modes in the late stages, implying that these perturbations decay without oscillation over time; the analytical findings also demonstrate that the brane structure primarily determines the distribution of the quasinormal spectrum while preserving the purely imaginary nature of the quasinormal frequencies. subsequently, we further simulate the gravitational wave signal by numerically evolving the perturbation equations, which yields late-stage results consistent with the analytical predictions. interestingly, these quasinormal modes carry information about the cosmological constant on the brane, which provides a potential new pathway for the study of cosmology in the ds brane scenario.

title: analytic gravitational wave spectrum in next-to-minimal bouncing cosmology
abstract: bouncing cosmology offers a singularity-free alternative to inflation. however, its minimal realization, known as minimal bouncing cosmology (mbc), comprises only four cosmic phases and produces a stochastic gravitational-wave background (sgwb) with a single power-law spectrum. interpreting the pulsar timing array (pta) signal within this framework faces tension with the $δn_{\rm eff}$ bound and has required trans-planckian bounce energies, restricting its observational viability. in this work, we propose next-to-minimal bouncing cosmology (nmbc) by adding an earlier phase of cosmic evolution to mbc. using our previously developed primordial gravitational-wave propagation-matrix method, with an improved matching prescription, we derive explicit analytic expressions for the resulting sgwb spectrum. the spectrum takes a broken power-law form: the low- and high-frequency tilts are determined by the equations of state of the additional and original contraction phases, respectively, while the spectral amplitudes depend jointly on these equations of state and the characteristic transition-time scales. this additional freedom allows a pta-band signal to coexist with a scale-invariant or red-tilted high-frequency branch, providing a way to satisfy the $δn_{\rm eff}$ bound. for the scale-invariant high-frequency branch, a pointwise benchmark using the adopted $δn_{\rm eff}$ radiation budget gives $ρ_{s\downarrow}^{1/4}\lesssim2.65\,m_{\rm pl}$, where $m_{\rm pl}$ is the reduced planck mass. this provides a conservative comparison estimate for the setup considered here, since integrating the spectrum over the adopted illustrative frequency interval gives a tighter bound. the resulting upper limit is therefore of order the reduced planck scale. please refer to the pdf for the full abstract.

title: closing the mass window for stupendously large black holes
abstract: we show that primordial black holes (pbhs) in the $\textit{stupendously large black hole}$ mass range ($m \gtrsim 10^{11}\,m_\odot$) produce isocurvature perturbations exceeding current $\textit{planck}$ cosmic microwave background limits, thereby excluding them as a significant dark matter component.

title: false alarm rates in detecting gravitational wave lensing from astrophysical coincidences: insights with model-independent technique glance
abstract: lensing of gravitational waves (gws) due to intervening massive astrophysical systems between the source and the observer is an inevitable consequence of the general theory of relativity, which can produce multiple gw events with overlapping sky localization error. however, the confirmed detection of such a unique astrophysical phenomenon is challenging due to several sources of contamination, ranging from detector noise to astrophysical uncertainties. robust model-independent search techniques that can mitigate noise contamination have been developed in the past. in this study, we explore the astrophysical uncertainty associated with incorrectly classifying a pair of unlensed gw events as a lensed pair and the associated false alarm rate (far) depending on the gw source properties. to understand the effect of unlensed astrophysical gw sources in producing false lensing detections, we perform a model-independent test using the pipeline glance on a simulated population of merging binary black holes (bbhs). we find that $\sim$ 0.01\% of the pair of events can be falsely classified as lensed with a lensing threshold signal-to-noise ratio of 1.5, appearing at a time delay between the pair of events of $\sim$ 1000 days or more. we show the far distribution for the parameter space of the gw source masses, delay time, and lensing magnification parameter over which the model-independent technique glance can confidently detect lensed gw pair with the current ligo detector sensitivity. in the future, this technique will be useful in understanding the lensing far for next-generation gw detectors, which can observe more gw sources.

title: beyond quasinormal modes: a complete mode decomposition of black hole perturbations
abstract: we show that retarded green's functions of black hole spacetimes can be expressed as a convergent mode sum everywhere in spacetime. at late times a quasinormal mode sum converges, while at early times a matsubara (or, euclidean) mode sum converges. the two regions are separated by a lightcone which scatters from the black hole potential. the matsubara sum is a fourier series on the euclidean thermal circle associated to the early time region. we illustrate our results for pöschl-teller, btz, and schwarzschild. in the case of schwarzschild, we express the branch cut contribution as a convergent sum of de sitter quasinormal modes as $λ\to 0^+$, and exploit recent exact solutions to the heun connection problem. in each case we analytically show convergence by studying the asymptotics of residue sums and also provide numerical demonstrations.

title: the terrell-penrose effect revisited and extended for black hole spacetime
abstract: half a century ago, terrell and penrose independently studied the visual appearance of a moving sphere and found that the visual distortion can be formulated by a conformal transformation on the observer's celestial sphere. in this study, we examine the terrell-penrose effect by considering the images of spheres in two contrasting cases: i) a static sphere in the view of a moving observer, and ii) a moving sphere in the view of a static observer. in these two cases, the images are expected to be identical for flat spacetime because of the principle of relativity. however, utilizing ray-tracing simulations, our results find that the images are distinct, and in case ii) the image distortion violates conformality. we also extend the studies to schwarzschild spacetime. in case i), we can obtain a natural extension, whereas in case ii), it is demonstrated that gravity introduces an additional influence on the images of moving objects.

title: non-singular cosmologies matching regular black holes
abstract: we construct a new non-singular cosmological model matched to a minkowski-core regular black hole by means of a modified oppenheimer--snyder framework. its dynamics in both dust-only and scalar-field scenarios is studied and compared with that of two other non-singular models as well as the classical standard cosmology. the results show that, although all three non-singular cosmologies share identical late-time behavior and allow for a natural embedding of inflation in the scalar-field setting, they exhibit qualitatively distinct non-singular features at very early times. for the new cosmology specifically, we also investigate the scenarios of other cosmological fluids and, more generally, of multiple coexisting fluids. this cosmological model is found to manifest an intriguing symmetry between its asymptotic past and future: without a cosmological constant both limits are asymptotically minkowski, whereas with a positive one both are asymptotically de sitter. furthermore, a dynamical stability analysis reveals that the asymptotic-past state of this model is a robust attractor, thereby requiring no extreme fine-tuning of the initial conditions.

title: a machian wave effect in conformal, scalar-tensor gravitational theory
abstract: woodward's simultaneous energy-density identities, imposed exactly with a constant physical speed of light and nonzero proper density, fix the potential and exclude the independent potential derivatives used in his derivation. a background interpretation instead requires the perturbation terms omitted by that derivation. in general relativity (gr), the second time derivative isolated from the exact landau-lifshitz equations belongs to the gravitational operator and supplies no additional material mass source. in the hoyle-narlikar (hn) derivation of woodward and fearn, the linear second time derivative cancels from the time-time component; the covariant trace cancels the squared-gradient terms retained in fearn's diagonal sum. their propulsion estimates contain further errors in mechanical power, momentum transfer and constitutive dimensions. the mechanical analysis retains damping, complex harmonic response and the dissipative energy and entropy balances. for a smooth strictly positive scalar, an admissible weyl transformation, universal material coupling and consistently mapped matter, driving and boundary data, the complete continuum conformal hn action becomes the einstein action. under these hypotheses, the additional measured force relative to the corresponding einstein result is identically zero for the same physical matter model. compatible global source-integral and absorber conditions restrict the admitted solutions and preserve this equality. woodward and fearn's mass-fluctuation and propulsion formulas do not follow from the stated gr or continuum conformal hn equations. their additional scalar propulsion force is excluded in the local continuum sector under the stated hypotheses.

title: superradiant scattering by rotating black-bounce black holes
abstract: we investigate superradiant scattering off a rotating regular black hole described by a black-bounce metric which generalizes the kerr spacetime of mass $m$ and specific angular momentum $a$ through a regularization parameter $p$ and two deformation exponents $(k,n)$. focusing on massless $(\ell,m)=(1,1)$ scalar modes, we explore the parameter space and compute amplification factors by numerically integrating the separated radial klein-gordon equation. we track the peak amplification and the corresponding frequency across the $(a/m,p/m)$ parameter space for several combinations of $k$ and $n$. we find that increasing $n$ systematically enhances superradiance, whereas increasing $k$ tends to suppress it. in particular, certain configurations can lead to amplification factors that significantly exceed the maximum amplification found for standard kerr black holes.

title: simultaneous determination of hubble constant and cosmic baryon density: forecasts for the synergy between frbs and emerging probes
abstract: two of the most pressing challenges in cosmology are the persistent discrepancy in measurements of the hubble constant, referred to as the hubble tension, and the deficit of baryons in the local universe, known as the missing baryon problem. fast radio bursts (frbs) provide a unique probe of both the hubble constant $h_0$ and the cosmic baryon density $ω_{\rm b}$. however, constraints from frbs alone suffer from a severe $h_0$-$ω_{\rm b}$ degeneracy that prevents them from resolving either problem. we show that this degeneracy can be broken by combining frbs with other emerging probes whose degeneracy directions differ in the $h_0$-$ω_{\rm b}$ plane. specifically, we quantify three multi-messenger approaches: frbs paired with gravitational wave (gw) standard sirens, strong gravitational lensing (sgl) time delays, and 21 cm intensity mapping (im) surveys. the combinations frb+gw, frb+sgl, and frb+21 cm im each deliver simultaneous constraints on $h_0$ and $ω_{\rm b}$ better than (1%, 1.5%) in the $λ$cdm model, and when dynamical dark energy is introduced, the constraining precision degrades gracefully as model complexity increases. furthermore, within a model-independent framework, both frb+gw and frb+sgl constrain $h_0$ and $ω_{\rm b}$ to precisions better than (1.5%, 3%). these precision levels are based on nominal observational expectations and would improve significantly under optimistic observational scenarios.

title: gravitational wave polarization modes and stability analysis in weyl geometry gravity
abstract: we investigate the gravitational wave polarization modes and stability in weyl geometry gravity within a minkowski background. our results indicate that the tensor sector consists of two standard modes propagating at the speed of light. although the vector sector possesses a dynamical perturbation, it generates no polarization modes. the scalar sector, in contrast, features a mixture mode of breathing and longitudinal modes associated with a single scalar degree of freedom. the propagating solutions of this scalar mode exhibit superluminal propagation and can undergo intrinsic amplitude decay, both of which are driven by the background weyl gauge field. we further discuss the observational detectability of this scalar mode. our stability analysis reveals that, while the tensor and vector sectors are free from ghost and laplacian instabilities, the scalar sector suffers from a ghost instability. these findings clarify the unique gravitational wave propagation characteristics in weyl geometry gravity and provide theoretical foundations for testing the theory through future multi-messenger observations.

title: towards a carrollian description of yang-mills
abstract: we provide a theory defined purely on null infinity that describes yang-mills in the minkowski space bulk. the dynamical field of our model is the characteristic data of the bulk gauge field, and the action combines an electric branch carrollian kinetic term with non-local interactions of mhv type that link different points on the celestial sphere. we explicitly show how this theory recovers all mhv and nmhv tree amplitudes in yang-mills, and outline how arbitrary tree amplitudes may be obtained from its feynman diagram expansion. the detailed expression we find for the nmhv amplitude appears to be new.

title: pole skipping, avoided crossing, and resonant excitation in kerr quasinormal modes near algebraically special frequencies
abstract: kerr quasinormal modes near algebraically special frequencies exhibit anomalous behavior, including apparent bifurcation, disappearance, and a nonsmooth connection to the schwarzschild limit, which has remained puzzling for decades. tracking poles and zeros of green-function building blocks across different riemann sheets, we show that the bifurcation is due to an avoided crossing accompanied by resonant excitation, while the disappearance is due to pole skipping caused by cancellation of a quasinormal-mode pole by a matsubara-mode zero. this resolves the physical origin of these long-standing anomalies.

title: non conservative conformal killing gravity: coupling the dark sector with curvature and matter
abstract: the so called harada gravity with non conserved energy-momentum tensor is here taken into account. it includes rastall gravity as a special case. the field equations are written as einstein equations where the source is supplemented by a divergence-free conformal killing tensor and a tensor proportional to the metric, linear in the scalar curvature and the trace of the energy-momentum tensor. these terms can be natural candidates for dark sector and give rise to a coupling of the dark sector with the matter content. the field equations are the conformal killing extension of rastall gravity, and include unimodular gravity. in a friedmann-robertson-walker background, the cosmic microwave background restricts parameters so that the dark sector only couples with the trace of the energy-momentum tensor. the explicit form of the tensor for the dark sector is found, and the friedmann and continuity equations are presented, with a standard cosmological analysis. the sum of energy-momentum tensors of dust matter and of dark fluid is conserved, and the dust energy density evolves with the scale function with exponent -3/(1+tau), modified by the coupling tau with the dark fluid.

title: shadow, emission, and strong-field lensing of dilatonic black holes
abstract: we study the shadow and strong-field optical properties of a static, spherically symmetric dyon-like dilatonic black hole. the photon sphere radius, critical impact parameter, and shadow radius are obtained and analyzed in terms of the charge $q$ and the dilatonic coupling parameter $a$. we show that increasing these parameters decreases the photon sphere and shadow radii, leading to a smaller apparent shadow. the predicted angular diameter is compared with the observational data for m87$^{*}$ and sgra$^{*}$. we explicitly show that the sgr a* data do not constrain the model parameters, whereas the results for m87* depend on the adopted mass estimates from stellar and gas dynamics. we also estimate the high-frequency energy emission rate in the geometric-optics approximation and derive the leading bozza coefficient $\bar{a}$, which characterizes the logarithmic behavior of the deflection angle in the strong-field regime. astrophysical implication of the obtained outcomes are discussed.

title: nonrotating and rotating black holes with secondary disformal hair in a ghost-free metric-affine parity-violating scalar-torsion theory
abstract: in this paper, we formulate a ghost-free metric-affine scalar-torsion model in which a pseudoscalar field is coupled to the nieh--yan density and derivatively coupled to the einstein-palatini tensor. the theory is projectively invariant and, in the shift-symmetric sector, depends on the scalar field only through its gradient. after fixing the projective gauge, the independent connection is solved exactly: its symmetric part is the levi-civita connection associated with the metric $h_{μν}$, disformally related to the metric $g_{μν}$, while its antisymmetric part is a purely axial torsion sourced by $v_μ=\partial_μ\vartheta$. we identify a degenerate ghost-free branch, $α=6β^2κ^2$, for which ricci-flat geometries in the $h$-metric frame solve the metric equations and the noether current vanishes identically. for example, we consider schwarzschild and kerr geometries in the $h$-metric frame, which generate disformal deformations on these geometries from the perspective of the $g$-metric frame. for the schwarzschild black hole in the $h$-metric frame, we construct static and babichev--charmousis-like time-dependent scalar profiles, and discuss horizon regularity in eddington--finkelstein coordinates. for the kerr black hole in the $h$-metric frame, we show that regularity on the rotation axis rules out a nontrivial globally real static fixed-norm scalar profile. for the stationary time-dependent branch, axis regularity and asymptotic reality fix $y_0=-q^2$ and eliminate the angular dependence, yielding a nontrivial future-regular profile in ingoing kerr coordinates. the kerr solution with the nontrivial scalar field is stealth only in the $h$-metric frame. in the $g$-metric frame, it produces disformal corrections stemming from the nontrivial scalar field profile and it represents secondary disformal scalar hair rather than primary noether-charge hair.

title: wave optics effects from gravitational wave propagation through dark matter halos
abstract: gravitational wave (gw) propagation is usually studied under the geometric optics approximation. however, when gws propagate through structures of sizes similar to their wavelength, this approximation breaks down. to study this situation, we present a scheme for numerically evolving linearised plane gws through stationary, spherical astrophysical structures in both weak and strong gravity regimes. our simulations evolve the full einstein equations (with all 10 components) for gaussian, nfw and burkert potentials. our simulations show that the scattering of the gws depends not only on the mass of the lens but also strongly on the gravitational potential distribution of the lens. among our most important results, we find that the gws do not propagate along null geodesics when propagating through the gaussian density, neither in the strong nor weak gravity setting. another significant finding is that in the strong gravity case of the burkert potential, the convexity of the wave is flipped when leaving the structure.   we compare our results with the linearized scalar wave predictions and find that the difference between these and the exact gw modes are of order one when the wave is inside the central potential. however, the difference reduces to only a few percent when the wave has passed through the structure. although these effects are small, future gw detectors and pulsar timing arrays (ptas) could be sensitive to these signals which could thus potentially help in constraining the structure of dark matter spikes or halos.

title: harmonic oscillation and orbital morphology for spinning charged quantum corrected black hole
abstract: this study investigates the dynamical behavior of particle's test around a spinning charged einstein-maxwell-dilaton (emd) quantum corrected black hole (qcbh) by examining the effects of spinning parameter $a$, quantum correction parameter $b$, and charge parameter $q$. using emd spacetime geometry, we analyze the effective potential and effective force to determine the stability and structure of the circular orbits in a strong gravitational field. furthermore, we calculate the oscillation frequencies radial $(ω_r)$, vertical $(ω_θ)$, and angular $(ω_ϕ)$, as well as the corresponding periapsis and lense-thirring precession frequencies. the spin parameter primarily determines the spinning properties of spacetime, while the quantum correction and charge particle introduce additional biases to kerr-newman geometry, particularly near the event horizon. these corrections alter the position and stability of the circular orbits, and the spectrum effectively associates with particle's motion. the results provide a comprehensive description of the orbital dynamics of spinning emd qcbh through future high-precision astrophysical observations.

title: octupole moments and the non-universality of free-fall in general relativity
abstract: extended bodies in general relativity do not necessarily fall along geodesics. instead, a body can experience accelerations that depend on its angular momentum, as well as on its quadrupole, octupole, and higher-order moments. moreover, due to the fact that one object's multipole moments can evolve differently from those of another, different bodies can fall differently---even with identical initial data. this paper examines how octupole moments contribute to the non-universality of free-fall in general relativity. we begin by showing that in arbitrary vacuum spacetimes, only the trace-free component of an octupole moment can affect an object's motion. it follows that at least 16 out of 40 octupole components decouple from the laws of motion. we also obtain two decompositions for trace-free octupole moments, one in terms of a timelike frame vector and the other in terms of a null tetrad. these decompositions are applied to motion both in static newtonian spacetimes and in fully-relativistic vacuum spacetimes that are of petrov type d (such as kerr). in newtonian spacetimes, the mass moments are shown to have their ordinary newtonian effects. the momentum moments instead determine a body's hidden momentum---the misalignment between its momentum and its velocity. in petrov type d spacetimes, we show that some torques that are impossible with quadrupole moments are generically possible with octupole moments. octupole moments can thus have qualitatively-different effects from quadrupole moments.

title: scalar perturbations and strong cosmic censorship for an asymptotically de sitter regular black hole
abstract: we investigate the quasinormal modes (qnms) of scalar perturbations and strong cosmic censorship (scc) in regular ayón-beato-garcía-bronnikov-de sitter (abgb-ds) black hole spacetime. the main motivation of this work is to clarify whether the regularization of black hole core, which removes the central singularity, can also change the fate of scc connected to the cauchy horizon. we first study the dependence of the scalar qnm frequency (qnf) on the scalar mass and black hole parameters. for angular number $l=0$, a small scalar mass can give rise to a slowly decaying mode which is purely imaginary, while it will become complex for large enough scalar mass and we call it ds-like mode. we also find that the black hole charge and cosmological constant affect the qnm spectrum in qualitatively opposite ways. we then examine scc under massless and massive scalar perturbations. for massless perturbations, the qnms spectrum can be organized into photon sphere (ps), de sitter (ds) and near-extremal (ne) families. compared with the scc in the reissner-nordström-de sitter (rn-ds) case, scc is generally more easily violated in the abgb-ds spacetime, although this tendency is reversed for sufficiently large cosmological constant. for massive scalar perturbations, we find that the scalar mass does not restore scc. instead, it can enhance the violation by driving the system into the regime $β>1$. at last, we discuss what we may expect from the violation of scc in a regular black hole spacetime.

title: static multipolar einstein-vector-gauss-bonnet black holes
abstract: we construct and analyze static multipolar black holes in einstein-vector-gauss-bonnet theory with a quadratic coupling function. the vectorized solutions bifurcate from the schwarzschild black hole at discrete values of the gauss-bonnet coupling, obtained from a perturbative eigenvalue problem on the schwarzschild background and labelled by the angular multipole number $\ell$. we restrict to the fundamental radial branches. the electric sector contains the known spherically symmetric $\ell=0$ branch as well as axisymmetric branches with $\ell>0$. these electric branches extend to larger values of the coupling. the magnetic sector features a sequence of axisymmetric branches, including the previously found magnetic dipole branch at $\ell=0$. the magnetic branches instead exist only on finite intervals of the coupling, ending at critical solutions. away from the bifurcation point, nonlinearities generate additional multipoles, but even-$\ell$ and odd-$\ell$ moments remain separated.

title: regular magnetic black holes with anti-de sitter cores in scalar-tensor gravity: axial stability and radial instability
abstract: we construct static, asymptotically flat regular black holes in einstein-frame scalar--tensor gravity, sourced by a canonical scalar coupled to magnetic nonlinear electrodynamics. prescribing the density and scalar profiles, we reconstruct the metric, the scalar--photon coupling and the potential. regularity requires the mass function to vanish at the centre, which fixes the adm mass, and the central $r^2$ growth of the density to be compensated by the gradient energy of the scalar. the solutions have an anti-de sitter core supported by a negative potential and a nearly reissner--nordström exterior; absence of ghosts restricts the magnetic charge to an interval that shrinks to zero at a finite core depth. axial perturbations reduce to a symmetric two-channel master system whose positive-definite potential guarantees mode stability; spectral and time-domain quasinormal frequencies agree. radial perturbations, by contrast, are unstable: the reconstructed potential behaves as $v\propto-φ^5$ near the asymptotic vacuum, the scalar becomes tachyonic outside the horizon, and every ghost-free black hole has a growing monopole mode with $γm\approx0.14$--$0.28$. an angular laplacian instability develops near the centre; for black holes it may lie entirely within the inner horizon, while horizonless solutions leave it uncovered and are therefore excluded.

title: draining without emptying a stringy black hole: repetitive electric penrose process
abstract: this paper studies the repetitive electric penrose process in the gibbons-maeda-garfinkle-horowitz-strominger (gmghs) black hole under the optimal condition for maximum energy extraction. unlike the reissner-nordström (rn) black hole, the effective potential curve of the incident particle in the gmghs black hole remains unchanged during the iterations. the iteration termination conditions are determined by two aspects: the escape condition requires that particle 0 can overcome the effective potential peak and escape to infinity, and this condition is independent of the black hole charge; the existence condition for negative-energy particle 1 requires the black hole charge to be sufficiently large, indicating that the repetitive process cannot completely consume the charge of the gmghs black hole to zero. numerical simulations show that the return on investment of energy extraction can exceed $100\%$, but the energy utilization efficiency does not exceed $50\%$, and most of the extractable energy is converted into an increase in the irreducible mass of the black hole. in addition, a smaller decay radius and a larger absolute value of the charge-to-mass ratio of particle 1 can improve the return on investment and energy utilization efficiency of energy extraction; the larger the specific energy of the incident particle, the smaller the return on investment of energy extraction, while the energy utilization efficiency remains unchanged; for an initially non-extremal black hole, as the initial charge increases, the return on investment of energy extraction increases monotonically, while the energy utilization efficiency first increases and then decreases. after the iterations end, the black hole still retains extractable energy, and neither the charge nor the mass vanishes.

title: creation of the universe in lorentzian classical gravity
