abstract: the singularity theorems and the past incompleteness of inflationary spacetimes suggest that the beginning of the universe lies beyond the domain of semiclassical gravity. we show that the creation of the universe can nevertheless be understood within lorentzian gravity by allowing gravitational junctions, so that the full spacetime need not be a smooth manifold. we construct rotationally invariant cosmic creation gates joining any finite number $n\geq2$ of locally de sitter regions in $d\geq3$ spacetime dimensions at a timelike perfect-fluid junction with $p=wρ$. for $w>-(d-3)/(d-2)$, they are geodesically complete in both temporal directions. the total spatial volume approaches finite, positive limits in the infinite past and future on the global-time foliation adapted to the junction fluid. we also construct exact deformed cosmic creation gates through nonlinear homogeneous backreaction that retain the initial volume while the future volume grows without bound. in these solutions, the junction fluid always expands, cooling for $w>0$ and heating for allowed $w<0$. keeping the bulk regions locally de sitter, we determine the linearized perturbations: in three dimensions, the generic inhomogeneous sector contains one hybrid sound mode and $n-1$ relative transverse modes; in four and higher dimensions, only the homogeneous hybrid sound mode survives. a finite-volume beginning requires fine-tuned homogeneous and inhomogeneous initial data, while causal response generically leads to unbounded future spatial volume. we also discuss a broader creation criterion allowing bounded past-volume oscillations. the gravitational equations determine conditioned admissible histories. we discuss implications for cosmology.

title: seeing unseen gravitational wave inspirals at the galactic center
abstract: the galactic center is expected to host a population of extremely large mass-ratio inspirals (x-mris) migrating toward the supermassive black hole. we propose an observational approach utilizing the secular gravitational torque exerted by x-mris on the highly eccentric s-star s301. this approach is intrinsically limited by the stochastic nature of the surrounding stellar-mass black hole cusp. as s301 propagates through this granular medium, it experiences discrete gravitational encounters. standard orbital fitting procedures inherently assume a smooth background potential; applying them to stochastic trajectories averages these discrete velocity discontinuities into a continuous secular drift. this introduces a systematic bias that mimics the x-mri precession signal, invalidating traditional mass estimation techniques. to resolve this degeneracy, we implement a methodology based on the wavelet transform modulus maxima method to characterize the local hölder regularity of the orbital motion. this model isolates the singular discontinuities induced by stellar-mass black hole encounters from the continuous torque of the x-mri distribution, allowing for detection even when instantaneous accelerations are below the instrumental noise threshold. we demonstrate analytically that s301 is highly sensitive to the interior x-mri population while remaining dynamically decoupled from the secular influence of the exterior cusp. combining precision astrometry and radial velocity projections, we establish that a minimal population of two x-mris is detectable within a five to nine-year timeframe, allowing us to constrain the presence of an unseen orbiter population prior to the launch of space-based gravitational wave detectors.

title: the redshift-space cluster-galaxy cross-correlation as a probe of gravity on cosmic scales
abstract: testing general relativity (gr) on cosmological scales requires probes that are directly sensitive to gravitational dynamics. we present a fisher matrix forecast of how well the dark energy spectroscopic instrument (desi) bright galaxy survey (bgs) can constrain departures from gr through the cluster infall velocity field, using the redshift-space cluster-galaxy cross-correlation function $ξ^{\rm s}_{\rm cg}(r_p, r_π)$ as the primary observable. we construct mock catalogs from the abacussummit n-body simulations, using a halo occupation distribution (hod) model for galaxies and a log-normal mass-observable relation for cluster selection. we parameterize departures from gr with a single multiplicative factor $f_{\rm g}$ that rescales halo infall velocities relative to the gr prediction. marginalizing over the hod, mass-observable, and cosmological parameters, we find that desi bgs can constrain $f_{\rm g}$ to $σ(f_{\rm g}) = 0.033$ at $z \sim 0.3$. this precision is sufficient to distinguish representative $f(r)$ and galileon gravity models from gr at $\gtrsim 4σ$. the strongest limitation is a degeneracy between $f_{\rm g}$ and the scatter in the cluster mass-observable relation, while the constraint shows no strong degeneracy with any individual hod parameter. perfect knowledge of the galaxy-halo connection would improve the constraint to $σ(f_{\rm g}) \approx 0.015$, and including the galaxy autocorrelation function in the data vector could recover part of this improvement. the same data vector yields tight constraints on the cosmological parameters, $σ(ω_m) = 0.010$ and $σ(σ_8) = 0.010$, only moderately correlated with $f_{\rm g}$. these results demonstrate the potential of desi bgs cluster-galaxy correlations to test gravity on quasi-linear scales, complementary to existing modified gravity probes and to weak-lensing cluster mass profiles.

title: considering numerical relativity surrogate models for agn channel merger dynamics
abstract: binary black hole mergers (bbh) are currently observed by the gravitational-wave detectors ligo, virgo, and kagra (lvk). a fraction of these mergers are likely to originate in active galactic nuclei (agn), but the details of the dynamical processes driving agn channel mergers remain poorly understood. monte carlo for agn channel testing and simulation (mcfacts) is an open-source, public software used to simulate agn channel bbh formation and evolution with configurable options for exploring various agn and nuclear star cluster (nsc) parameter options. within mcfacts, bbh mergers evolve through gas drag and dynamical interactions, ignoring relativistic effects which can influence merger remnant properties. here we demonstrate in mcfacts the effect of handing off inspiralling bbh to a numerical relativity (nr) surrogate model, which more accurately predicts the masses, spins, and kick velocities of merger remnants. compared to a simple analytic approach to calculating merger and remnant properties the nr surrogate model is significantly more accurate at predicting remnant spins, which improve $χ_{eff}$ and $χ_{p}$ calculations, and recoil kicks, parameters especially important for higher generation bbh mergers. our findings show the nr surrogate significantly changes distributions of remnant spins and kick velocities, as well as showing that alternative methods should be used cautiously in future studies. we also outline some simple models which are computationally efficient and can reproduce much of the nr surrogate model results.

title: inverse design of scalar-tensor eft from odd-parity effective potentials
abstract: we develop an inverse-design approach to the effective field theory (eft) of perturbations in scalar-tensor gravity around static and spherically symmetric backgrounds with a timelike scalar-field gradient, taking the odd-parity effective potential as input and reconstructing compatible background and eft data. as analytically tractable examples, we construct explicit realizations of the pöschl-teller potential, for which the quasinormal-mode spectrum can be obtained in closed form. we then study the regge-wheeler potential of general relativity and its parametrized deformations, showing how both can be realized within the scalar-tensor eft. in particular, the latter realizations provide a route to interpreting phenomenological constraints on potential deformations from black hole ringdown observations in terms of the underlying eft data.

title: apparent horizon mergers in analytic intial data
abstract: five years ago pook-kolb, hennigar and booth published a series of three papers exploring the evolution of apparent horizons and other marginally outer trapped surfaces during a black hole merger. this was seen to be much more intricate than the well-known "pair-of-pants" merger associated with event horizons. in this paper we show that parameter evolutions of brill-lindquist-desitter initial data mimic many of the features of that evolution. hence, this analytic intial data is a useful testing ground for ideas about marginally outer trapped surface evolution and spacetime geometry during mergers.

title: search for eccentric neutron star-black hole binaries in advanced ligo's fourth observing run using effective-one-body waveforms
abstract: the observation of orbital eccentricity in compact binary coalescences would provide a direct signature of dynamical formation environments. previous matched-filter searches for eccentric neutron star-black hole (nsbh) binaries have been severely limited by computational constraints, necessitating the use of simplified waveform models that capture secular dephasing but omit apsidal precession and inter-orbit harmonics. including these physical features increases the sensitive search volume for systems with $0.2 \le e_{20} \le 0.28$ by $\sim 25\%$ to $30\%$. we present a rapid matched-filter search methodology that makes the direct use of time-domain effective-one-body waveforms computationally feasible. by multibanding and high-frequency ratio-filtering, our pipeline achieves a $\sim 20\times$ reduction in computational cost. this allows a bank of 88.6 million effective-one-body templates, fifteen times larger than prior eccentric analyses, to search o4a and o4b advanced ligo data. we recover the known low-mass mergers gw230518_125908 and gw230529_181500 with parameters consistent with zero eccentricity. finding no new gravitational-wave events with orbital eccentricity ($e_{20} \ge 0.05$), we place $90\%$ credible upper limits on the local merger rate density of eccentric nsbh systems across the search space of $\mathcal{r}_{90\%} \le 7.5\text{-}57\ \mathrm{gpc}^{-3}\ \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, up to a factor of $\sim 4$ improvement over previous observational bounds. at the parameters of gw200105_162426, this non-detection establishes an upper limit of $\mathcal{r}_{90\%} \le 12.1\ \mathrm{gpc}^{-3}\ \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$. alternatively, if gw200105_162426 is treated as an eccentric detection, the lack of subsequent detections in o4 updates the inferred local merger rate density of this population to $\mathcal{r} = 6.6^{+6.3}_{-3.8}\ \mathrm{gpc}^{-3}\ \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$.

title: physical effects in the vicinity of black holes
abstract: general relativity, a theory that is already over a century old, is still the best theory that we have to describe the universe at energy scales where only the gravitational force is important. it has stood tall to any observational tests thrown at it since its inception, and it has remarkable predictive power when it is utilized to study and model astrophysical problems. it also continues to surprise us with its ability to generate new problems and insights that render themselves useful in the study of modern physics. this is especially highlighted by the transition of modern observational astronomy away from an electromagnetic radiation epoch, and into a new gravitational wave epoch. this thesis devotes its study to phenomena that can be analyzed within the framework of classical general relativity, but whose results may contain interesting implications for cosmological and black hole observations. (full abstract can be found in document).

title: axion-angle dependence of the rotational and tidal properties of pnjl quark stars
abstract: we investigate how a fixed, spatially uniform axion angle modifies the rotational and static tidal properties of self-bound quark stars in general relativity, using an axion-extended polyakov-loop nambu--jona-lasinio equation of state. we vary $θ$ from $0$ to $π$ while holding the remaining model parameters fixed, and compute the leading-order moment of inertia and the second-order spin-induced quadrupole moment and mass shift. the calculation includes finite-surface-density contributions to the rotational mass shift and static tidal response. across this range, the static maximum mass increases from $1.68$ to $1.95\,m_\odot$, remaining below the lower edge of the quoted $1σ$ timing interval for psr~j0740+6620. at $m=1.338\,m_\odot$, the moment of inertia increases by $13\%$ and the dimensionless tidal deformability rises from $342$ to $547$. over the common mass range examined, the differences in the moment of inertia between adjacent sampled angles exceed the tested interpolation and table-resolution sensitivities. despite these changes, joint fits to the five sequences describe the $\bar i$--$c$ and i-love-q relations with maximum departures of $2.7\%$ and $0.4\%$, respectively, over the fitted domains. the predicted binary tidal-deformability curves lie within the estimated 90\% credible region of the adopted gw170817 posterior over the mass-ratio ranges examined. within this eos family, stellar properties vary appreciably with $θ$, while the normalized quantities admit accurate joint fits across the five sequences.

title: hamiltonian analysis of the newer general relativity
abstract: we present a systematic hamiltonian analysis of the five-parameter class of theories known as newer general relativity. quadratic nonmetricity theories of this type can be divided into nine types according to the structure of their primary constraints. after reviewing the framework of symmetric teleparallel gravity, we derive the adm formulation of newer general relativity, discuss the existing classification and perform the hamiltonian formulation of the theory. for each type, we compute the conjugate momenta, identify the primary constraints, and construct both the canonical and primary hamiltonians. we then determine the constraint structure and analyze the resulting physical degrees of freedom in each type.

title: quasinormal modes of a rotating hořava black hole: two perturbative approaches to nonseparability
abstract: quasinormal modes (qnms) provide a powerful probe of strong-field gravity. we study fundamental scalar quasinormal modes of an asymptotically flat rotating black hole in the low-energy sector of hořava gravity, whose exact scalar equation is nonseparable due to rotation-induced lorentz violation. we develop two complementary approximations that both preserve the exact kerr sector: method i applies a slow-rotation approximation only to the nonseparable lorentz-violating part, whereas method ii employs a small-$η$ biorthogonal spheroidal projection, with $η$ the lorentz-violating parameter. using residual-controlled continuation and symmetric finite differences, validated by a kerr continued-fraction benchmark and an independent radial spectral method, we compute the linear frequency response. axisymmetric modes provide an exact kerr null test. for the corotating modes studied, the real-frequency response is positive and increases with spin. at $a/m=0.9$, the two methods reveal a roughly $2\%$ angular correction to the real response, while the imaginary response is nonmonotonic and highly sensitive to angular projection due to internal cancellation. these results highlight the distinct rotational signatures of lorentz violation in black-hole ringdown.

title: the non-relativistic limit of five-dimensional boson stars and scale invariance violation
abstract: we investigate the non-relativistic limit of spherically symmetric boson stars in (4+1)-dimensional general relativity (gr). in this limit, the resulting newtonian theory exhibits an exact scale invariance, leading to a critical boson star configuration with a fixed global u(1) charge and vanishing binding energy. we identify the origin of these properties in the restored scale symmetry and analyze how relativistic and gravitational corrections break this symmetry. by comparing the full (4+1)-dimensional einstein-klein-gordon system with the wick-cutkosky model, we quantify the effects of these corrections on the energy-charge relation and the kinematic stability of the configurations. our results demonstrate how weak violation of scale invariance lifts the degeneracy of the non-relativistic solutions and determines the behavior of boson stars away from the critical limit.

title: resonance correction to time-dependent finite-size effects in effective field theory of binary black hole inspiral
abstract: general relativity predicts that black holes lack an internal structure and that their tidal love numbers vanish. however, if astrophysical black holes were instead ultra-compact objects (ucos) with internal structure, their tidal love numbers would no longer vanish. then, during a binary inspiral, their tidal deformation could transfer orbital energy to the uco, increasing the orbital period and leaving an observable imprint on the phase of the emitted gravitational waves. as we discussed previously, the effect is enhanced if one binary companion is resonantly excited. here we use the point-particle effective field theory framework to calculate this enhancement. we consider circular orbits and focus on excitations of the internal electric quadrupole, modelling the uco spectrum as a harmonic oscillator spectrum. however, our methods could be straightforwardly extended to more complicated situations. integrating out the internal quadrupole induces a series of time-dependent finite-size operators with specific numerical coefficients, which we calculate. we find that the static electric quadrupole love number $k_2$ is negative, and that all finite-size terms are proportional to $k_2$. we further show that resonant excitation induces a leading 2.5 post-newtonian term, compared with the 5 post-newtonian term in the time-independent case. our results confirm the expectation that resonant excitation during a binary inspiral offers one of the best ways to detect whether astrophysical black holes can undergo tidal deformation and, if they do, learn about their internal excitation spectrum.

title: gravitational field of spinors with torsion and matter$-$antimatter asymmetry
abstract: the conservation law for the orbital plus spin angular momentum of a free dirac particle in curved spacetime requires that the affine connection has the antisymmetric part: the torsion tensor, which extends general relativity to the einstein$-$cartan theory of gravity. in spacetime with torsion, the dirac equation becomes a nonlinear, cubic equation in the spinor wave function. under charge conjugation, the nonlinear term changes sign relative to the mass term. a dirac spinor and its charge conjugate therefore satisfy different field equations. we use the spinor connection formalism to derive the dirac equation for a spherical spinor in its centrally symmetric gravitational field with torsion. we determine the energy$-$momentum tensor for this spinor and show that the energy contribution from torsion is negative for matter particles and positive for antimatter particles. consequently, the ground state of a fermion has a lower energy than the ground state of the corresponding antifermion. we also derive the einstein$-$cartan$-$dirac equations for this spinor; they indicate the existence of particle-like soliton solutions exhibiting matter$-$antimatter energy asymmetry.

title: isospectrality breaking in the axial quasinormal modes of reissner-nordström black holes in dynamical chern-simons gravity
abstract: we study odd-parity perturbations of reissner-nordström black holes in dynamical chern-simons gravity. the dcs action is parity invariant because $\vartheta\,{}^{*}rr$ is the product of two pseudoscalars; nevertheless, the pseudoscalar perturbation has odd parity and enters only the axial sector at linear order and so lifts the axial--polar isospectrality of general relativity. we derive the finite-charge couplings between the pseudoscalar and the axial gravitational and electromagnetic perturbations directly from the linearized field equations. both directions are governed by the radial kernel $(mr-q^2)δ/r^8$, and at nonzero charge the pseudoscalar couples to $ψ+χψ_e$, with $χ=2q/[r\sqrt{(l-1)(l+2)}]$. after diagonalizing the einstein--maxwell sector, we compute branch-resolved quasinormal-mode shifts with exterior complex scaling for the photon-sphere modes and frobenius shooting for the near-extremal zero-damping modes. for the schwarzschild $l=2$ fundamental mode we obtain $β\,δω=-0.7733-0.3946\,i$ (units $m=α=1$). off resonance, the gravitational-led shift scales as $ζ\,l^3$ at $q=0$ but as $ζ\,l^2/q$ at fixed nonzero charge and large $l$. the electromagnetic-led branch becomes exactly degenerate with the pseudoscalar mode at $q_c=2m\sqrt{l(l+1)+1}/[l(l+1)+2]$, where the pseudoscalar potential coincides with the polar partner of the electromagnetic-led potential; there the breaking is $\mathcal{o}(\sqrtζ)$, $m|δω|\simeq2.4\sqrtζ$ for $l=2$, and the shift reverses sign across $q_c$. near extremality the photon-sphere shifts remain finite, whereas the non-degenerate fundamental gravitational-led zero-damping mode is suppressed, $δω/ω\simeq6.0\times10^{3}\,ζ\,(1-q^2/m^2)$ for $l=2$.

title: unifying stochastic and deterministic signals: a practical search for the intermittent binary black-hole background
abstract: over the past decade, the advanced ligo, advanced virgo, and kagra detectors have detected nearly 400 compact binary mergers, most of which are stellar-mass binary black-hole (bbh) mergers. nevertheless, most mergers in the universe are too weak to be individually detected at current sensitivity levels. since a bbh merger in band is much shorter than the average time between successive mergers, the population of these subthreshold events gives rise to an intermittent background of gravitational waves (gws). this gw background is guaranteed to exist, but it has not yet been detected with current stochastic or deterministic searches. here we propose a fast and accurate likelihood-based search for this background, which unifies the standard model-agnostic cross-correlation search and a fully deterministic, template-based search in a single likelihood. our search is based on a truncated likelihood ratio, which is fully marginalized over the extrinsic parameters of the individual mergers, and which represents the data in two detectors as an expansion in terms of approximate sufficient statistics. these statistics are higher-order cross-moments of the data, weighted by geometrical factors that generalize the standard overlap reduction function (orf) used in cross-correlation searches. we show that almost all the bayesian evidence and information on the bbh merger population comes from correlations between frequency bins induced by individual mergers and is captured in the higher-order generalized orfs. consequently, any likelihood function that does not take these inter-frequency correlations into account is necessarily suboptimal. we validate our search on one year of simulated advanced ligo data, and find that a catalog-informed analysis, which uses information from both the detected and unresolved mergers, can infer the peak of the redshift distribution of the population of bbh mergers.

title: integrable singularities obstruct cauchy horizons and mass inflation
abstract: black-hole interiors with an inner (cauchy) horizon are unstable through the poisson-israel-ori mass-inflation mechanism, governed by the dray-'t hooft-redmount relation and widely regarded as a dynamical realization of strong cosmic censorship. we show that static, spherically symmetric anisotropic interiors supported by a marginally divergent but integrable density $ρ\sim a/r^2$, with $a>1/(8π)$ and mild screening at finite radius, are incompatible with this mechanism. the compactness $q=m/r$ decreases monotonically from a super-critical central value to $1/2$ at the unique event horizon, producing a strictly positive compactness gap throughout the trapped region and excluding any second zero of the lapse. this gap enters the dynamics quantitatively. (i) under the null energy condition and a dynamical screening condition, $2m/r$ is non-decreasing along both future null directions of a trapped domain, so the gap propagates under nonlinear spherically symmetric evolution. (ii) for ingoing radiation (generalized vaidya), the gap bounds the blueshift: the advanced time spent in the gapped region is finite, whereas it diverges at a cauchy horizon. (iii) for counter-streaming null dust, the radiative part $μ$ of the misner-sharp mass obeys exactly $\partial_u\partial_vμ=2\,\partial_uμ\,\partial_vμ/(r|f|)$, of which the dtr relation is the thin-shell form; the in-out coupling $2/(r|f|)$ is uniformly bounded on the interior precisely when the gap is positive. this yields an a priori mass bound and, in the ori thin-shell model, an e-folding rate bounded by the influx luminosity instead of tending to the inner-horizon surface gravity. integrable-singularity interiors thus realize a class of sources for which the poisson-israel-ori amplification channel is structurally inoperative in the models in which mass inflation was originally established.

title: probing scalar polarization with next-generation gravitational-wave detectors: the roles of detector geometry and source inclination
abstract: gravitational-wave observations of compact binaries offer a direct way to test whether gravity admits polarizations beyond the two tensor modes of general relativity. we perform a forecast to assess how well future multi-messenger events will constrain the presence of scalar polarizations in gravitational waves. performing binary neutron star injections, we forecast next-generation constraints on three modified gravity parameters in the ppe formalism: $α$ (tensor amplitude), $α_b$ (scalar amplitude) and $β$ (tensor and scalar phase). cosmic explorer (ce) and einstein telescope (et) each tighten every parameter by 1--2 orders of magnitude over an o5 ligo-virgo network, with et's triangular geometry giving a persistent $\approx2\times$ improvement over 2$\times$ce on the scalar-mode amplitude $α_b$ in both a gw170817-like and a second, representative bns. we show that, if the sky position and luminosity distance are known from em observations, adding an em-based prior on the orbital inclination $ι$ narrows the $α_b$ constraint by $\approx56\times$ relative to an isotropic inclination prior, for a gw170817-like event. we also assess how em inclination priors as well as assumptions on the neutron star equation of state may affect the inference on the scalar amplitude $α_b$. overall, these results indicate that detector geometry and the availability of well-placed em external information are both important levers --- alongside raw network sensitivity --- for next decade scalar-polarization tests.

title: early-time tails in kerr black hole ringdown
abstract: black hole ringdowns are modelled as a superposition of quasinormal modes (qnms), although the branch cut of the green's function produces a nonoscillatory tail that may contaminate early-time ringdown analyses. within linear perturbation theory, we quantify this branch-cut contribution for the scattering of localised gaussian wave packets by a kerr black hole with mass $m$. defining the onset of ringdown as the earliest time at which the qnm and branch-cut contributions reconstruct the waveform, we evaluate the branch-cut amplitude relative to the qnm amplitude. for wave packets with a characteristic frequency $ω_0\sim 1/m$, the branch-cut amplitude is typically of order $10\%$ of the qnm amplitude at ringdown onset with only a mild dependence on spin. we further find that the tail waveform before convolving with a source is almost independent of spin. the spin dependence of the relative amplitude therefore resides primarily in the excitation of the qnms. our results suggest that the branch-cut contribution may affect the accuracy of black hole spectroscopy, particularly near the onset of ringdown.

title: complete quasinormal modes of type-d black holes. ii. extremal kerr black holes
abstract: we develop a double-confluent heun (heund) method that extends our construction of complete quasinormal-mode (qnm) spectra to extremal kerr black holes. matching the horizon-ingoing and infinity-outgoing radial solutions together with angular regularity yields the frequencies directly at extremality, without extrapolation from nonextremal spins. for gravitational perturbations, we obtain an expanded spectrum on both conventional and unconventional riemann sheets, including additional qnms revealed by analytic continuation across frequency branch cuts. continuation in spin connects the extremal modes to our complete schwarzschild spectrum, including its unconventional branches. we show for the first time that unconventional class i sequences with $m<0$, continued from unconventional schwarzschild modes, approach negative superradiant bounds with vanishing damping in the extremal limit. we also identify finite-damping modes interspersed among sequences approaching zero damping, showing that a single overtone cutoff cannot describe the transition to extremality. independent scattering-amplitude calculations verify representative frequencies and their sheet assignments, while a contour count establishes spectral completeness within a bounded frequency domain. uniform matching near the superradiant bound further distinguishes critical accumulation from isolated extremal qnms and resolves the associated riemann-sheet structure. these results bring extremal kerr into our unified treatment of black-hole qnm spectra and reveal how the schwarzschild mode families reorganize in the extremal limit.

title: gravitational lensing of gravitational waves by a kerr black hole
abstract: we simulate the gravitational lensing of gravitational waves (gws) by a kerr black hole using a $(1+1)$-dimensional time-domain mode-sum approach. to enable efficient explicit time evolution, we implement a localized hyperboloidal foliation combined with a static field redefinition, ensuring bounded characteristic speeds across an extended, uniform tortoise-coordinate grid. incident gw initial data are constructed by projecting a plane-wave weyl tensor onto the kinnersley tetrad. through local spin-dyad rotations and wigner $d$-matrix transformations, our framework accommodates both idealized wave packets and realistic binary coalescence signals at arbitrary incidence and polarization angles. to accurately resolve the lensed waveforms, we evolve over $68,000$ coupled $(j,m)$ modes. our results reveal that a kerr black hole acts as a diffraction-limited thick lens, focusing gws into a forward beam. for idealized wave packets, the primary prompt pulse exhibits a spin-independent transverse gaussian profile, whereas the subsequent lensing coda is sensitive to the black hole's spin. for binary coalescence signals, strong-field lensing substantially modifies the post-merger ringdown. however, the lensed inspiral and merger phases in kerr and schwarzschild backgrounds are virtually identical, yielding waveform mismatches below $2.2\times10^{-5}$ across various inclinations and polarizations. these findings demonstrate that non-spinning schwarzschild models provide an accurate and computationally economical surrogate to search for strong-field lensing signatures with current ground-based detectors.

title: energy-flux noise induced by imperfections of the gaussian beam in the li-baker hfgw detector
abstract: this paper investigates the energy-flux noise induced by imperfections of the gaussian beam (gb) in the li-baker high-frequency gravitational wave (hfgw) detector. modeling these imperfections with higher-order laguerre-gaussian (lg) beams, we analytically derive the resulting noise-to-signal ratio for both co- and cross-polarized $\mathrm{lg}_{nl}$ modes. it is found that higher-order co-polarized lg beams generate no tangential energy-flux noise at the optimal detection plane ($ϕ=π/2$ or $3π/2$), whereas higher-order cross-polarized lg beams introduce non-negligible noise. specifically, for an individual higher-order cross-polarized $\mathrm{lg}_{nl}$ mode under our representative parameters, maintaining the noise-to-signal ratio below unity typically requires the power fraction to satisfy $σ_{nl}<10^{-46}$, with the $\mathrm{lg}_{01}$ mode imposing the most stringent constraint of $σ_{01}<6.0\times10^{-49}$. monte carlo simulations suggest that the total power fraction $σ_{\mathrm{total}}$ of multiple higher-order cross-polarized $\mathrm{lg}_{nl}$ modes needs to remain below $10^{-49}$. consequently, we propose employing a polarization filter to retain only the co-polarized component of the gb adopted in the practical experiment, thereby suppressing the noise while preserving signal integrity. these results provide theoretical guidance for noise control in the li-baker hfgw detector.

title: scalar-induced gravitational waves in spatially covariant gravity with two tensorial degrees of freedom
abstract: we study scalar-induced gravitational waves (sigws) in a spatially covariant gravity model with two tensorial degrees of freedom, minimally coupled to a $k$-essence scalar field. for the parameter choice considered during radiation domination, the quadratic tensor action coincides with that of general relativity (gr). we derive the scalar transfer functions at finite $σ\equiv c_2\bar n$ and in the large-$|σ|$ limit. we then construct the source function of sigws. we further examine a cubic extrinsic-curvature interaction that modifies the source function of sigws without affecting the background or quadratic actions. we calculate the fractional energy density of sigws for monochromatic and log-normal primordial curvature power spectra. we find that, for the positive values of $σ$ studied, finite-$σ$ effects suppress the spectrum over a broad range of scales relative to the result in the $σ\rightarrow \infty$ limit. in this limit, the cubic interaction suppresses the spectrum at small wavenumbers and enhances it at larger wavenumbers. these results show that modified scalar dynamics and non-linear interactions can alter the fractional energy density of sigws even when the quadratic tensor action is identical to that of gr.

title: radial pulsations of gravitationally decoupled anisotropic self-bound stars with a generalized linear equation of state
abstract: we construct anisotropic self-bound stellar configurations through gravitational decoupling in the minimal geometric deformation framework and investigate their stability against linear radial perturbations. retaining the tolman iv temporal potential, we impose the generalized linear equation of state $p_r=η(ρ-ρ_s)$ on the complete matter distribution. central regularity and schwarzschild matching determine the radial geometry and relate the surface density to the compactness and stellar radius. closed-form solutions are obtained for $η=1,1/2,1/3,1/4$, including the mit bag radial relation when $η=1/3$ and $ρ_s=4b$. since the equilibrium anisotropy does not determine its dynamical response, we introduce two material prescriptions that preserve either the anisotropy of each fluid layer or its ratio to $ρ+p_r$. including metric perturbations, we compute the fundamental mode and three overtones for twelve equilibrium configurations under both prescriptions. all 24 background response combinations have positive fundamental squared frequencies, establishing linear radial stability within the adopted closures. the fundamental eigenvalue decreases with compactness within each sampled family, while changing the anisotropic response produces shifts whose direction depends on the background. tangential tensions in several configurations and the failed tangential profile diagnostic of the maximally stiff family limit their physical interpretation. these results provide analytically tractable self-bound backgrounds and demonstrate that identical equilibrium configurations can support distinct radial spectra depending on their anisotropic material response.

title: emergence of an acoustic black hole in a lattice model
abstract: we build an acoustic black hole in a lattice model: a draining vortex evolved by the local collide-and-stream rule of a lattice-boltzmann model, with no acoustic metric imposed, the geometry being measured from the steady state. a horizon emerges, first located from the measured mach profile and then confirmed by phonon ray tracing on the measured metric, and the ringdown after a perturbation follows approximately the quasinormal frequencies of the draining bathtub. the residual departures are traced to the cell-scale structure of the horizon, which is not an ideal absorber. we model it in two ways: as a reflective horizon on the ideal bathtub, with two free parameters (the modulus and phase of the reflectivity), and as the sonic point of the realised flow absorbing in its own frame, with no adjustable parameter. the second describes the horizon and the non-rotating spectrum best. superradiance has two ingredients: the emergent geometry, which amplifies in a loss-free calculation on the measured metric, and the horizon, whose absorption frame sets the width and strength of the amplified band but leaves no trace in the ringdown. both models are used to examine superradiance, which has not been observed in the present toy model: whether the lattice hole superradiates dynamically remains open. the lattice leaves its own imprint as well: a fourfold anisotropy of the sonic surface and a surface gravity set by the cell-scale structure of the horizon.

title: horizon residues, matter-trace winding and test-scalar modes in f(q,t) gravity
abstract: we extend the analysis of local horizon remnants in quadratic non-metricity gravity to a specific matter trace theory with the functional form f(q) = q + alpha q^2 + 16 pi lambda t. here, the matter trace is defined by contracting the energy-momentum tensor with the metric from the original matter action. in the absence of explicit lambda-corrections, the theory inherits the vacuum logarithmic-connection hairy branch. to obtain a non-zero trace, we introduce polynomial non-linear electrodynamics and construct an exact magnetic branch in coincident cartesian kerr-schild coordinates. the non-metricity scalar of this branch vanishes, while its matter trace is proportional to the inverse eighth power of the distance. its metric component function is given by 1 - 2m/r + q^2/r^2 + c/r^6, where the correction term c equals xi(1 - 4 lambda)q^4 / 10. consequently, the quadratic non-metricity coupling is sterile on this branch. we derive the metric and matter equations, the euclidean temperature, the single-horizon remnant, the master scalar equation, and the first-order gauge shift. the logarithmic derivative of the matter trace imparts a winding number of -8 on a closed contour enclosing the central singularity, but a winding number of zero on a sufficiently small horizon contour. nevertheless, the temperature and scalar propagation still vary continuously with the correction coefficient. therefore, the trace winding number classifies divisor data rather than superseding the matter trace or determining its backreaction. this analysis also demonstrates a degeneracy between the trace coupling coefficient and the non-linear electromagnetic coefficient. these results are specific to this particular branch; this paper does not expound upon the full coupled gravity spectrum, nor does it claim priority for this magnetic metric.

title: quasinormal modes of slowly rotating black holes in hernquist halos: redshift and angular momentum
abstract: we investigate axial quasinormal modes of black holes embedded in hernquist halos, using an established analytic static geometry with an inner vacuum cavity extending to $4m_{\mathrm{bh}}$ and solving for frame dragging to first order in rotation. we compute the fundamental and first overtone branches for mass ratios $ε\equiv m_{\mathrm{bh}}/m_{\mathrm{halo}}$ of $0.1$ and $0.01$, and halo compactness $\mathcal c\equiv m_{\mathrm{halo}}/a_0$ in the range $10^{-4}\leq\mathcal c\leq0.3$. the cavity geometry gives a local kerr estimate in which redshift rescales the vacuum frequencies, horizon angular momentum sets the rotational splitting, and uniform frame dragging adds a real frequency shift. at zero spin, the cavity redshift reproduces the complex $\ell=2$ frequencies with relative residuals below $0.04\%$ for the fundamental and $0.31\%$ for the first overtone. its leading weak compactness behavior, $1-\mathcal c$, explains the weak mass ratio dependence in dilute halos; at larger compactness, the exact redshift accounts for most of the separation between the two mass ratio sequences. at fixed total angular momentum, halos with vanishing local angular momentum and those with vanishing coordinate angular velocity exhibit opposite compactness trends in the real spin coefficient. at $\mathcal c=0.3$, their real fundamental mode spin coefficients differ by approximately $38\%$ and $54\%$ for the two mass ratios. fixing the horizon angular momentum reduces these differences below $1\%$ for both overtones, showing that angular momentum partition accounts for most of the configuration dependence.

title: the pointing error due to laser propagation in space plasma for tianqin gravitational wave detection
abstract: tianqin, a space-borne gravitational wave observatory, is designed to detect gravitational-wave signals via laser interferometry. as the inhomogeneous space plasma surrounds the inter-satellite laser links, the propagation of the laser in space plasma can introduce pointing error noise. in this work, we quantitatively assess the effect of plasma on the pointing accuracy of tq's inter-satellite laser links. we employ a magnetohydrodynamic model to simulate the plasma distribution around the tq orbit for different orbital orientations. using the fourth-order runge-kutta method to conduct the ray-tracing calculations over a tq orbital cycle under a solar wind dynamic pressure close to the 23-year average, we find that the plasma-induced laser deflection angle and pointing eccentricity are on the order of $10^{-20} \ \mathrm{rad}$ and picometers, respectively. these values are significantly lower than tq's requirements. our results demonstrate that the impact of space plasma on tq's pointing error is negligible in moderate space weather conditions, indicating a positive outlook for the tq mission.

title: searching for axion-like particles with space-based optical lattice clock networks
abstract: axion like particles (alps) are particularly well motivated candidates for dark matter, and physics beyond the standard model more generally. however, direct detection remains extremely challenging due to the weakness of their interactions. in this work, we propose to employ space-based optical lattice clock networks (solcn), originally targeted to probe the stochastic gravitational wave background (sgwb), to detect axion dark matter through cosmic birefringence via minor modifications to their laser links. searching for cross-correlated signals then provides significant sensitivity to low mass alps as a result of their large correlation lengths. in this work we focus on alps in the mass range $10^{-18.55}\text{ev}-10^{-14}\text{ev}$, for alps mass region $10^{-18}-10^{-14}\text{ev}$, finding that we can probe down to $g_{aγ}\geq 10^{-12}\,\text{gev}^{-1}$. moreover, we find that the solcn sensitivity to the alp-photon coupling depends crucially on the frequency of the network link. with an $8$ ghz frequency link, we then have the potential to reach $g_{aγ}\geq10^{-16}\,\text{gev}^{-1}$ in this region.

title: quasinormal mode excitation in the horizon shear of near-extremal kerr black holes
abstract: the horizon shear of a near-extremal kerr black hole perturbed by an eccentric extreme mass ratio inspiral shows low amplitude, high frequency oscillations (''wiggles") after periapsis passage. previous works are unable to tie the frequency of the wiggles to the orbit, and argue they cannot be quasinormal modes (qnms). we show that they are kerr qnms belonging to the damped-mode branch --- that is, modes whose decay rate stays finite as the spin approaches extremality. for an equatorial prograde orbit with $p = 3m$ and $e = 0.85$ and spins ranging from $a/m = 0.999$ to $a/m = 0.99999$, fits to the time-domain shear identify the fundamental $(\ell,m) = (2,1)$ and $(3,2)$ modes as the dominant and first subdominant excitations. fitting each multipole separately gives frequencies to within two standard deviations of the kerr values and provides evidence for the excitation of the fundamental $(3,1)$, $(4,1)$ and $(4,2)$ modes, though these are not resolvable in the full signal. we further argue that the same wiggles must be present in the tidal field that drives the shear. for $\ell \leq 4$ we find no evidence of qnm excitation in the $m = 0$ or the $m = \ell$ multipoles.

title: topological interpretations in anisotropic kerr-newman-ads black hole thermodynamics
abstract: the interplay between black hole thermodynamics and topology provides a strong, coordinate-independent framework for discovering the underlying structure of black hole phase transitions as well as their universal features. we explore the thermodynamic topology of the anisotropic kerr-newman-ads black hole using duan's $ϕ$-mapping theory and a complex residue approach. by creating the generalized off-shell free energy, we propose a thermodynamic vector field in the parameter space with zero points corresponding to equilibrium black hole states. the winding numbers associated with these defects are utilized to calculate the black hole's global topological number. we begin with an analysis of the entire anisotropic kerr-newman-ads black hole, followed by two limiting examples. setting the anisotropic parameter $k = 0$ produces the kerr-newman-ads black hole, while eliminating the ads contribution produces the kerr-newman black hole. the anisotropic kerr-newman-ads and kerr-newman-ads black holes have a single thermodynamic defect with winding number $+1$, which results in $w = +1$. in contrast, the kerr-newman black hole has two defects with winding numbers $+1$ and $-1$, which result in a vanishing global topological number, $w = 0$. these findings show that the ads contribution alters the global topological classification, but the anisotropic matter studied here preserves the topological class of the kerr-newman-ads black hole. as an analogous limiting instance, we further study a kiselev-type black hole, analyzing the circumstances in which its metric reduces to a charged black-hole geometry and how the thermodynamic topology reflects this reduction. finally, we use the complex residue approach on the anisotropic kerr-newman-ads black hole.

title: robust statistical significance for gravitational wave inference
abstract: the field of gravitational-wave data analysis heavily relies on bayes factors to make statements about astrophysical effects in events detected by the ligo-virgo-kagra collaboration. this is true on an event level, for example when discussing the potential detection of precession or eccentricity, as well as on a population level. for the latter, perhaps the main limiting factor is the reliance on the output from event-level nested sampling analyses, which is known to introduce growing uncertainties and biases as the number of detections increases. in both cases, while bayes factors are useful when comparing different models, because the underlying distribution of bayes factors in noise is unknown, it is often not possible to use them to make quantifiable statistical statements. their statistical meaning is also questionable in the at least $20\%$ of gravitational-wave events that contain transient noise artifacts. this paper shows that it is possible to use evidence networks, which can infer bayes factors after learning the distinguishability between datasets, to solve all of the aforementioned problems. by being able to calculate up to $10^5$ bayes factors per second, we can construct background distributions of bayes factors under different signal assumptions to estimate significance. we show that the high precision achieved allows us to scale the results from up to $10^4$ events with no discernable bias on population-level quantities, while laying the foundations for a likelihood-free method that does not rely on the assumption of gaussian and stationary noise.

title: raki: high-order alternative finite differences for general relativistic magnetohydrodynamics
abstract: binary neutron star (bns) and black hole--neutron star mergers are among the most important multimessenger sources. observations of these events could provide valuable insights into several unresolved phenomena, ranging from the efficiency of magnetic field amplification during and after mergers to the formation of magnetars and jets. understanding these phenomena requires accurate modelling of magnetic field evolution, which remains a challenge for state-of-the-art general relativistic magnetohydrodynamics (grmhd) simulations. in this work, we present \texttt{raki} (relativistic astrophysics code implementation of the alternative finite difference approach for grmhd), the first grmhd code to simulate bns mergers using high-order alternative finite-difference methods with adaptive-order weno (afd-weno-ao) reconstruction and a fully non-staggered, node-centred vector-potential formulation. the code achieves up to ninth-order convergence in smooth test problems while accurately capturing discontinuities. in magnetised tolman--oppenheimer--volkoff (tov) star tests, \texttt{raki} retains $99.2$ per cent of the initial maximum magnetic field strength over ${\sim}2$ ms, exhibiting an order of magnitude less magnetic field loss than a reference grmhd code at the same resolution. in bns merger simulations, fifth-order afd-weno-ao reconstruction yields approximately third-order convergence of the gravitational-wave phase in both magnetised and unmagnetised models. the discrete no-monopole constraint is preserved to machine precision without staggered grids, even during bns mergers with moving refinement regions. these results establish \texttt{raki} as a high-order, non-staggered grmhd framework for accurate modelling of magnetic field evolution in neutron star mergers and its implications for multimessenger astrophysics.

title: self-bound anisotropic stars in $\mathcal{r}+α\mathcal{r}^2$ gravity with a hayward exterior: junction conditions and nicer constraints
abstract: analytic compact-star models in modified gravity usually borrow the junction conditions of general relativity and fix their constants with radii derived for a particular stellar model. here we avoid both. we study $\mathcal{f}(\mathcal{r})=\mathcal{r}+α\mathcal{r}^{2}$ gravity with a durgapal-bannerji interior of embedding class one (karmarkar condition) and a hayward exterior. without birkhoff's theorem, the exterior is an assumption, and we measure its effect with the hayward metric, which deforms schwarzschild by a length $\ell$. the junction conditions of quadratic $\mathcal{f}(\mathcal{r})$ gravity fix all constants in closed form in terms of $m$, $r$ and $\ell$. the condition $p_r(r)=0$ is replaced by continuity of the trace of the extrinsic curvature. the ricci scalar jumps at the surface, so there is a thin shell with negative surface energy density for $α>0$, a gravitational double layer, and a small radial stress. for this stress to be below 1% of the central pressure we need $α\lesssim0.2$ km$^{2}$ and $\ell\lesssim0.3m$. the interior behaves as a self-bound star. a single surface energy density, $ρ_s=(1.37\pm0.16)ρ_0$, reproduces psr j0740+6620, j0437-4715, j0030+0451 and j0614-3329, and for $α=0.1$ km$^{2}$ the model predicts $r_{1.4}=11.5$ km and a maximum mass of $2.9 m_\odot$. because $\ell$ enters surface observables only at order $(\ell/m)^{2}(m/r)^{3}$, the results carry over to a schwarzschild exterior. calibrating instead with strange-star radii of eclipsing x-ray pulsars gives $r_{1.4}\approx9$ km, which current data rule out.

title: diamonds in the sky: the shape of gravitational waves from cosmic string cusps
abstract: we carry an in-depth analysis of the gravitational wave (gw) emission of cosmic string cusps, going beyond the seminal work of damour and vilenkin. we identify two features that, to the best of our knowledge, have not been described in the literature: first the gws emission from a cusp, at any given frequency, is not concentrated inside a cone but instead draws a diamond-like shape in the sky. second, the emission is not maximal in the direction of the cusp velocity, but in two slightly offset directions. we explain these effects in detail, and illustrate them with simplified examples. then, we study two limiting cases for which the overall radiated power is enhanced: when the diamond is stretched in a particular direction, and when higher order derivatives vanish at the cusp. we statistically estimate the importance of these effects in a population of odd-harmonic loops.

title: phenomenological implications of cosmic (super)strings with time-varying tension
abstract: cosmic strings and cosmic superstrings could have formed in the early universe. in a particular class of models, the tension associated with these defects is time dependent, either because the strings themselves are composed of evolving moduli fields, or because they are directly coupled to evolving scalar fields leading to an effective time dependence in the string tension. here we take seriously the possibility of this time dependence and investigate the phenomenological consequences of such an evolution, comparing the results to the more traditional case of a fixed time independent tension. in particular, for five different time varying models, motivated by different possible forms of evolution of the string tension, we evaluate their gravitational wave (gw) contributions as well as their impact on the cosmic microwave background (cmb). performing an mcmc analysis of the models we find there are indeed interesting spectral signatures in the gw emission at frequencies between the current pta and interferometer data, but the signatures are not unique to these strings, making them hard to pin down using current data. however, we do find cosmic strings with evolving tension fit the gw data as well as other favoured models.

title: inverse gertsenshteǐn-zel'dovich effect in time-independent electromagnetic field
abstract: the inverse gertsenshteǐn-zel'dovich effect describes the conversion of gravitational waves into electromagnetic waves in the presence of a background electromagnetic field. this effect has primarily been studied for constant background electromagnetic fields. in this work, we develop a general formalism for calculating the components of the electric and magnetic fields induced by the passage of a gravitational wave through a spatially varying, time-independent background electromagnetic field. the formalism accommodates all six possible polarization modes of gravitational waves. we illustrate its applicability through several examples, including gravitational waves propagating through constant and spatially varying electromagnetic fields. we further investigate the electromagnetic signals generated by the passage of gravitational waves through astrophysical magnetic fields, particularly those associated with neutron stars and magnetars. by connecting gravitational waves and electromagnetic waves--two essential messengers of multi-messenger astronomy--the inverse gertsenshteǐn-zel'dovich effect offers a promising framework for both gravitational-wave detection and astrophysical observations. the formalism developed here may therefore find applications in the design of high-frequency gravitational-wave detectors and in the investigation of high-energy astrophysical electromagnetic signals.

title: curvature scaling and linear area response in charged black-hole interiors
abstract: we identify the mechanisms and range of validity of two scaling laws reported in charged black-hole interiors. in spherical evolutions with a neutral massless scalar, mass inflation produces a large internal mass $m$, followed by a plateau. small scalar and electric corrections give $k\simeq48m^2/r^6$, where $r$ is the areal radius and $k$ the kretschmann scalar. the local exponent is near six when the mass and relative curvature correction also vary slowly with radius. the exact bound $k\geq28q^4/(5r^8)$, with $q$ the charge, excludes a finite-coefficient $r^{-6}$ asymptote, while a large plateau mass delays electric corrections to $r\sim q^2/m$. for sufficiently large plateau mass, this classical regime can reach planckian curvature before electric corrections become significant. at fixed coordinates and initial gauge, a linear response of $ρ=r^2$ to the initial scalar amplitude $a$ gives the half-power radius law near a simple zero. where both mechanisms apply, $k/m^2\propto(a_*-a)^{-3}$, with $a_*$ the area zero. full evolutions confirm the electric correction, support the half-power law at several observation times, and test the joint inverse-cube law.

title: photon rings and mass-independent observables of a five-dimensional charged ads black hole
abstract: we investigate the optical properties of a five-dimensional charged anti-de sitter (ads) black hole. using the null geodesic equations, we determine the event horizon and photon sphere radii and the critical impact parameter, showing that all decrease with increasing charge, while the photon sphere radius remains independent of the ads radius. to avoid dependence on the mass scale and the observer-dependent apparent size of the shadow in an ads spacetime, we introduce two mass-independent geometric observables: the subring exponent $γ$ and the ratio of the critical impact parameter to that of the direct image of the innermost stable circular orbit (isco). we derive $γ$ in closed form and show that it is independent of the ads radius and satisfies $2π/\sqrt{3}<γ\leqπ\sqrt{2}$, above the values for four-dimensional schwarzschild and reissner--nordström black holes. using a markov chain monte carlo (mcmc) forecast based on noiseless mock data with illustrative fractional uncertainties of $5\%$, we find that the dimensionless ads radius can be constrained with a relative uncertainty of $16$--$19\%$, whereas the charge can be distinguished from zero only for the near-extremal fiducial model considered. under these assumptions, the subring exponent provides a gaussian separation of $3.4$--$5.9σ$ from the four-dimensional schwarzschild black hole.

title: disentangling spin-induced precession vs. eccentricity in gw190521 and gw231123
abstract: we use the more than 2000 full numerical-relativity simulations included in the fifth release of the rit binary-black-hole waveform catalog to perform bayesian parameter estimation, via the rapid iterative fitting algorithm (rift), for the gravitational-wave events gw190521 and gw231123. we revisit gw190521, which has previously been identified as potentially possessing large eccentricity upon entering the detector band at $20~\mathrm{hz}$, and confirm this finding: the highest likelihood is obtained from waveforms that are simultaneously eccentric and spin-precessing, yielding $e_{20} =0.207_{-0.147}^{+0.192}$ and $χ_{1,\perp}=0.717_{-0.406}^{+0.194}$. applying the same simulation pool to gw231123, we likewise find a preference for spin precession where at 20 hz $χ_{1,\perp}=0.678_{-0.462}^{+0.218}$, but in this case with negligible eccentricity at both $10~\mathrm{hz}$ and $20~\mathrm{hz}$, with $e_{10}=0.097_{-0.073}^{+0.124}$ and $e_{20}=0.056_{-0.045}^{+0.059}$. for comparison, both events are also analyzed using exclusively non-precessing (eccentric and quasi-circular) simulations, which yield lower likelihoods in each case. these results indicate that our approach is capable of discriminating between the effects of eccentricity and spin precession in current gravitational-wave signals. the singled out top peak likelihood nr simulations give estimates of the recoil velocities of the merged final holes of 3965km/s for gw190521, and of 2059km/s for gw231123.

title: the effective kerr-compton tree amplitude from black hole perturbation theory
abstract: we develop a new method to construct the tree-level compton amplitude for gravitational-wave scattering off a kerr black hole in post-minkowskian effective field theory. building on previous computations that required physical consistency of the amplitude, the method uses wave scattering functions from black hole perturbation theory to uniquely determine additional contact terms. we illustrate the iterative procedure by deriving explicit expressions up to sixth order in spin, including previously unknown sectors at the fifth and sixth orders in spin. the amplitude features complex transcendental structures and a leading dissipative contact term at sixth order in spin. we verify our result against known results in the literature and reproduce the one-loop tail result from black hole perturbation theory.

title: rotation overcharges vectorized black holes
abstract: a charged black hole has a ceiling: extremality bounds the charge that a given mass and spin can support. vector hair has so far only lowered it. in the einstein--maxwell--vector (emv) model, where a massless vector field couples nonminimally to the electromagnetic invariant, the spherically symmetric vectorized reissner--nordström black holes are strictly undercharged: vector hair is paid for in charge. whether this ceiling is a property of the vector field or merely of spherical symmetry has remained open, because spherical symmetry hides the hair's mass as well: its komar mass vanishes identically and the exact identity $m_v=2ω_hj_v$ degenerates to $0=0$. rotation lifts both degeneracies at once. we construct the rotating solutions of the model, the first in this setting, and find that the hair's mass is not a free parameter but a second-order invariant of the rotational response, fixed by $m_v=2ω_hj_v$. above a coupling threshold the ceiling gives way: the domain of existence crosses the extremal kerr--newman bound, reaching $q=q/m>1$ with $q^2+χ^2$ up to $1.84$, while at $α=5$ the maximum charge stays below it. the shadow is where the hair becomes visible. at $(q,χ)=(0.9947,0.10)$, near the extremal bound, the hair contributes an ellipticity of $8.30\%$, against $0.44\%$ from the charge and $0.06\%$ from rotation --- a factor of $19$ that charging a kerr black hole cannot mimic; at the overcharged solution $(q,χ)=(1.2527,0.10)$ the total ellipticity reaches $25.6\%$. whether the branch is ghost-free remains open, but the existing no-go criteria do not settle it: they assume a background and a dispersion relation that do not hold here.

title: gravitational waves away from a schwarzschild black hole: full spectrum analysis
abstract: gravitational waves as one approaches schwarzschild null infinity are the core of our investigation, treated as the spin-weighted generalisation of a massless scalar field. in particular, we compute their full spectrum, consistent with observations coming from ligo and virgo experiments. this paper continues recent work by the authors, where the poincaré asymptotic expansion was exploited in black hole perturbation theory. the mathematical formalism we developed is now intimately connected with gravitational wave phenomenology, providing new mathematical tools to investigate their features.

title: curvature blindness: material inference in stars and black hole candidates
abstract: gravitational observations can leave material properties undetermined in two different ways: distinct states can have the same total source, and distinct spacetime histories can have the same retained observations. we organize these inverse problems in general relativity through a property-level identifiability criterion, with applications to stars and black hole candidates. two ideal massless gases illustrate equal-source ambiguity: their temperatures differ by a factor of $(8/29)^{1/4}$ and their entropies differ while their stress-energy tensors agree. a separate causal-fluid example starts with identical sources and geometric data but different constitutive responses; the two models' curvature histories separate at linear order in proper time and their scale factors at cubic order. for black hole candidates, the relevant distinction is between stationary exterior parameters, perturbing fluxes and constituent history. the framework provides a test for whether retained data identify a material property, separating instantaneous source equality, history-wide source equality and observational projection.
